566: func exposedPortsAttributeValue(ports []*clabtypes.GenericPortBinding) string {
567: 	if len(ports) == 0 {
568: 		return ""
569: 	}
570: 
571: 	sortedPorts := make([]*clabtypes.GenericPortBinding, 0, len(ports))
572: 	for idx := range ports {
573: 		if ports[idx] != nil {
574: 			sortedPorts = append(sortedPorts, ports[idx])
575: 		}
576: 	}
577: 
578: 	if len(sortedPorts) == 0 {
579: 		return ""
580: 	}
581: 
582: 	sort.Slice(sortedPorts, func(i, j int) bool {
583: 		left := sortedPorts[i]
584: 		right := sortedPorts[j]
585: 
586: 		switch {
587: 		case left.ContainerPort != right.ContainerPort:
588: 			return left.ContainerPort < right.ContainerPort
589: 		case left.Protocol != right.Protocol:
590: 			return left.Protocol < right.Protocol
591: 		case left.HostPort != right.HostPort:
592: 			return left.HostPort < right.HostPort
593: 		default:
594: 			return left.HostIP < right.HostIP
595: 		}
596: 	})
597: 
598: 	result := make([]string, 0, len(sortedPorts))
599: 	for idx := range sortedPorts {
600: 		formatted := formatExposedPort(sortedPorts[idx])
601: 		if formatted != "" {
602: 			result = append(result, formatted)
603: 		}
604: 	}
605: 
606: 	if len(result) == 0 {
607: 		return ""
608: 	}
609: 
610: 	return strings.Join(result, ";")
611: }
612: 
613: func formatExposedPort(port *clabtypes.GenericPortBinding) string {
614: 	if port == nil {
615: 		return ""
616: 	}
617: 
618: 	proto := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(port.Protocol))
619: 	protoSuffix := ""
620: 	if proto != "" {
621: 		protoSuffix = "/" + proto
622: 	}
623: 
624: 	if port.HostPort > 0 {
625: 		hostIP := port.HostIP
626: 		if hostIP == "" {
627: 			hostIP = "0.0.0.0"
628: 		}
629: 
630: 		if strings.Contains(hostIP, ":") {
631: 			hostIP = fmt.Sprintf("[%s]", hostIP)
632: 		}
633: 
634: 		if port.ContainerPort > 0 {
635: 			return fmt.Sprintf(
636: 				"%s:%d%s->%d",
637: 				hostIP,
638: 				port.HostPort,
639: 				protoSuffix,
640: 				port.ContainerPort,
641: 			)
642: 		}
643: 
644: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d%s", hostIP, port.HostPort, protoSuffix)
645: 	}
646: 
647: 	if port.ContainerPort <= 0 {
648: 		return ""
649: 	}
650: 
651: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%d%s", port.ContainerPort, protoSuffix)
652: }

40: // containerTracker turns the node states of the labs in an event scope into the container
41: // events the Docker runtime emits for the same lifecycle: create and start when a node's pod
42: // starts, kill, stop and die when it stops (on request, or between the pods of a restart),
43: // destroy when the node is removed, and health_status as its device becomes ready.

50: // trackContainers reports the container events of a scope. It reads the labs once, reporting
51: // them as a snapshot when the stream includes the initial state, and then reads a lab again
52: // whenever its Topology, Nodes or pods change. Changes that arrive together are read once.
53: func (r *Runtime) trackContainers(
54: 	ctx context.Context,
55: 	scope eventScope,
56: 	includeInitialState bool,
57: 	changed <-chan labRef,
58: 	eventSink chan<- clablabruntime.Event,
59: 	errSink chan<- error,
60: ) {
61: 	tracker := &containerTracker{r: r, sink: eventSink, nodes: map[string]*trackedContainer{}}
62: 
63: 	states, err := r.labStates(ctx, scope)
64: 	if err != nil {
65: 		sendEventError(ctx, errSink, err)
66: 		return
67: 	}
68: 	for _, state := range states {
69: 		tracker.observeLab(ctx, labRef{namespace: state.Namespace, lab: state.Name}, state,
70: 			&observeSeed{snapshot: includeInitialState})
71: 	}
72: 
73: 	pending := map[labRef]bool{}
74: 	timer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
75: 	timer.Stop()
76: 	defer timer.Stop()
77: 	armed := false
78: 	arm := func(delay time.Duration) {
79: 		if !armed {
80: 			timer.Reset(delay)
81: 			armed = true
82: 		}
83: 	}
84: 
85: 	for {
86: 		select {
87: 		case <-ctx.Done():
88: 			return
89: 		case ref := <-changed:
90: 			pending[ref] = true
91: 			arm(containerRefreshDelay)
92: 		case <-timer.C:
93: 			armed = false
94: 			refs := pending
95: 			pending = map[labRef]bool{}
96: 			for ref := range refs {
97: 				if !tracker.refresh(ctx, ref) {
98: 					pending[ref] = true
99: 				}
100: 			}
101: 			if len(pending) != 0 {
102: 				arm(containerRefreshRetryDelay)
103: 			}
104: 		}
105: 	}
106: }

114: // refresh reads a lab again and reports what changed for its nodes. A lab that is gone reports
115: // its nodes as destroyed. It returns false when the lab could not be read.
116: func (t *containerTracker) refresh(ctx context.Context, ref labRef) bool {
117: 	state, err := t.r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
118: 		Name:      ref.lab,
119: 		Namespace: ref.namespace,
120: 	})
121: 	if err != nil {
122: 		var notFound *labNotFoundError
123: 		if !errors.As(err, &notFound) {
124: 			if ctx.Err() == nil {
125: 				log.Debug("Failed to read a C9s lab for container events",
126: 					"namespace", ref.namespace, "lab", ref.lab, "error", err)
127: 			}
128: 
129: 			return ctx.Err() != nil
130: 		}
131: 		state = nil
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	t.observeLab(ctx, ref, state, nil)
135: 
136: 	return true
137: }

139: // observeLab compares the nodes of a lab with what was reported before and reports the
140: // difference. A nil state removes every node of the lab.

145: 	seed *observeSeed,

147: 	seen := map[string]bool{}

150: 			key := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, state.Nodes[idx].Name)
151: 			seen[key] = true
152: 			t.observeNode(ctx, ref, state, state.Nodes[idx], seed)
153: 		}
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	for key, tracked := range t.nodes {

160: 
161: 		for _, action := range containerRemovalActions(tracked) {
162: 			t.emit(ctx, tracked.lab, tracked.node, action, nil)
163: 		}
164: 		delete(t.nodes, key)
165: 	}
166: }

202: 	}
203: }
204: 
205: // containerHealth is the health a running node reports: a node that was healthy and is not
206: // ready anymore in the same pod is unhealthy, as a container whose healthcheck starts failing.
207: func containerHealth(previous, next *trackedContainer, health string) string {
208: 	if next.state != clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {
209: 		return ""
210: 	}
211: 	if health == "" {
212: 		health = clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting
213: 	}
214: 	if health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting && previous != nil &&
215: 		previous.state == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning && previous.pod == next.pod &&
216: 		(previous.health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy ||
217: 			previous.health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthUnhealthy) {
218: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthUnhealthy
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	return health
222: }
223: 
224: // containerTransitionActions are the container event actions Docker reports when a container
225: // goes from the previous to the next state:
226: //
227: //	new node            create (+ start when it runs, + stop when it is already stopped)
228: //	created -> running  start
229: //	exited  -> running  start
230: //	running -> exited   kill, stop, die (stop, or the old pod of a restart ending)
231: //	running -> created  kill, stop, die (the replacement pod of a restart not running yet)
232: //	running, new pod    kill, stop, die, start (restart)
233: //	created -> exited   stop
234: //
235: // A started node also reports its health (health_status: starting or healthy), and a running
236: // node reports health changes, like a container with a healthcheck.
237: func containerTransitionActions(previous, next *trackedContainer) []string {
238: 	const (
239: 		created = clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
240: 		running = clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
241: 		exited  = clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
242: 	)
243: 
244: 	var actions []string
245: 	previousState := ""
246: 	if previous != nil {
247: 		previousState = previous.state
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	switch {
251: 	case previous == nil:
252: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionCreate)
253: 		switch next.state {
254: 		case running:
255: 			actions = append(actions, containerActionStart)
256: 		case exited:
257: 			actions = append(actions, containerActionStop)
258: 		}
259: 	case previousState == running && next.state == running && previous.pod != next.pod:
260: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionKill, containerActionStop, containerActionDie,
261: 			containerActionStart)
262: 	case previousState == running && next.state != running:
263: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionKill, containerActionStop, containerActionDie)
264: 	case previousState != running && next.state == running:
265: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionStart)
266: 	case previousState == created && next.state == exited:
267: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionStop)
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	if next.state != running {
271: 		return actions
272: 	}
273: 
274: 	started := len(actions) != 0 && actions[len(actions)-1] == containerActionStart
275: 	if !started && previous != nil && previous.health == next.health {
276: 		return actions
277: 	}
278: 	if next.health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting && !started {
279: 		return actions
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	return append(actions, containerActionHealthPrefix+next.health)
283: }
284: 
285: // containerRemovalActions are the actions Docker reports when a container is removed: a running
286: // one is killed and dies first.
287: func containerRemovalActions(previous *trackedContainer) []string {
288: 	if previous.state == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {
289: 		return []string{containerActionKill, containerActionDie, containerActionDestroy}
290: 	}
291: 
292: 	return []string{containerActionDestroy}
293: }
294: 
295: // containerActionState is the container state after an action, which every container event
296: // reports in its state attribute.
297: func containerActionState(action, snapshotState string) string {
298: 	switch action {
299: 	case containerActionCreate:
300: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
301: 	case containerActionStop, containerActionDie, containerActionDestroy:
302: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
303: 	case containerActionStart, containerActionKill:
304: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
305: 	}
306: 	if strings.HasPrefix(action, containerActionHealthPrefix) {
307: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	return snapshotState
311: }
312: 
313: func (t *containerTracker) emit(
314: 	ctx context.Context,
315: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
316: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
317: 	action string,
318: 	extra map[string]string,
319: ) {
320: 	t.r.sendEvent(ctx, t.sink, c9sContainerEvent(state, node, action, extra))
321: }
322: 
323: // c9sContainerEvent is a container event of a node. The actor is the node, as for its interface
324: // events; its ID is the container_id inspect reports. Lab and Node let the events command
325: // describe the node with the attributes inspect and the Docker runtime report.
326: func c9sContainerEvent(
327: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
328: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
329: 	action string,
330: 	extra map[string]string,
331: ) clablabruntime.Event {
332: 	key := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)
333: 	attributes := map[string]string{
334: 		"namespace":                  state.Namespace,
335: 		"lab":                        state.Name,
336: 		"node":                       node.Name,
337: 		containerEventAttributeState: containerActionState(action, node.ContainerState),
338: 	}
339: 	if node.Pod != "" {
340: 		attributes["pod"] = node.Pod
341: 	}
342: 	if action == containerActionKill {
343: 		// Kubernetes stops a pod's containers with SIGTERM.
344: 		attributes["signal"] = containerEventSignalSIGTERM
345: 	}
346: 	for k, v := range extra {
347: 		attributes[k] = v
348: 	}
349: 
350: 	nodeCopy := node
351: 
352: 	return clablabruntime.Event{
353: 		Timestamp:   time.Now(),
354: 		Type:        clablabruntime.EventTypeContainer,
355: 		Action:      action,
356: 		ActorID:     key,
357: 		ActorName:   fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", state.Name, node.Name),
358: 		ActorFullID: key,
359: 		Attributes:  attributes,
360: 		Lab:         state,
361: 		Node:        &nodeCopy,
362: 	}
363: }

Changes that arrive together are read once.\nfunc (r *Runtime) trackContainers(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tscope eventScope,\n\tincludeInitialState bool,\n\tchanged <-chan labRef,\n\teventSink chan<- clablabruntime.Event,\n\terrSink chan<- error,\n) {\n\ttracker := &containerTracker{r: r, sink: eventSink, nodes: map[string]*trackedContainer{}}\n\n\tstates, err := r.labStates(ctx, scope)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tsendEventError(ctx, errSink, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tfor _, state := range states {\n\t\ttracker.observeLab(ctx, labRef{namespace: state.Namespace, lab: state.Name}, state,\n\t\t\t&observeSeed{snapshot: includeInitialState})\n\t}\n\n\tpending := map[labRef]bool{}\n\ttimer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)\n\ttimer.Stop()\n\tdefer timer.Stop()\n\tarmed := false\n\tarm := func(delay time.Duration) {\n\t\tif !armed {\n\t\t\ttimer.Reset(delay)\n\t\t\tarmed = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-ctx.Done():\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase ref := <-changed:\n\t\t\tpending[ref] = true\n\t\t\tarm(containerRefreshDelay)\n\t\tcase <-timer.C:\n\t\t\tarmed = false\n\t\t\trefs := pending\n\t\t\tpending = map[labRef]bool{}\n\t\t\tfor ref := range refs {\n\t\t\t\tif !tracker.refresh(ctx, ref) {\n\t\t\t\t\tpending[ref] = true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif len(pending) != 0 {\n\t\t\t\tarm(containerRefreshRetryDelay)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// observeSeed marks the first observation of a stream: it records the node states without\n// reporting changes, and reports them as a snapshot when asked to.\ntype observeSeed struct {\n\tsnapshot bool\n}\n\n// refresh reads a lab again and reports what changed for its nodes. A lab that is gone reports\n// its nodes as destroyed. It returns false when the lab could not be read.\nfunc (t *containerTracker) refresh(ctx context.Context, ref labRef) bool {\n\tstate, err := t.r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{\n\t\tName:      ref.lab,\n\t\tNamespace: ref.namespace,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tvar notFound *labNotFoundError\n\t\tif !errors.As(err, &notFound) {\n\t\t\tif ctx.Err() == nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.Debug(\"Failed to read a C9s lab for container events\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"namespace\", ref.namespace, \"lab\", ref.lab, \"error\", err)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\treturn ctx.Err() != nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tstate = nil\n\t}\n\n\tt.observeLab(ctx, ref, state, nil)\n\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// observeLab compares the nodes of a lab with what was reported before and reports the\n// difference. A nil state removes every node of the lab.\nfunc (t *containerTracker) observeLab(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tref labRef,\n\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState,\n\tseed *observeSeed,\n) {\n\tseen := map[string]bool{}\n\tif state != nil {\n\t\tfor idx := range state.Nodes {\n\t\t\tkey := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, state.Nodes[idx].Name)\n\t\t\tseen[key] = true\n\t\t\tt.observeNode(ctx, ref, state, state.Nodes[idx], seed)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor key, tracked := range t.nodes {\n\t\tif tracked.ref != ref || seen[key] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tfor _, action := range containerRemovalActions(tracked) {\n\t\t\tt.emit(ctx, tracked.lab, tracked.node, action, nil)\n\t\t}\n\t\tdelete(t.nodes, key)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (t *containerTracker) observeNode(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tref labRef,\n\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState,\n\tnode clablabruntime.NodeState,\n\tseed *observeSeed,\n) {\n\tkey := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)\n\tprevious := t.nodes[key]\n\tif node.ContainerState == \"\" {\n\t\tnode.ContainerState = clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated\n\t}\n\tnext := &trackedContainer{\n\t\tref:   ref,\n\t\tstate: node.ContainerState,\n\t\tpod:   node.Pod,\n\t\tlab:   state,\n\t\tnode:  node,\n\t}\n\tnext.health = containerHealth(previous, next, node.Health)\n\tt.nodes[key] = next\n\n\tif seed != nil {\n\t\tif seed.snapshot {\n\t\t\tt.emit(ctx, state, node, next.state, map[string]string{\n\t\t\t\t\"origin\": clablabruntime.EventOriginSnapshot,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, action := range containerTransitionActions(previous, next) {\n\t\tt.emit(ctx, state, node, action, nil)\n\t}\n}\n\n// containerHealth is the health a running node reports: a node that was healthy and is not\n// ready anymore in the same pod is unhealthy, as a container whose healthcheck starts failing.\nfunc containerHealth(previous, next *trackedContainer, health string) string {\n\tif next.state != clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tif health == \"\" {\n\t\thealth = clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting\n\t}\n\tif health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting && previous != nil &&\n\t\tprevious.state == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning && previous.pod == next.pod &&\n\t\t(previous.health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy ||\n\t\t\tprevious.health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthUnhealthy) {\n\t\treturn clablabruntime.ContainerHealthUnhealthy\n\t}\n\n\treturn health\n}\n\n// containerTransitionActions are the container event actions Docker reports when a container\n// goes from the previous to the next state:\n//\n//\tnew node            create (+ start when it runs, + stop when it is already stopped)\n//\tcreated -> running  start\n//\texited  -> running  start\n//\trunning -> exited   kill, stop, die (stop, or the old pod of a restart ending)\n//\trunning -> created  kill, stop, die (the replacement pod of a restart not running yet)\n//\trunning, new pod    kill, stop, die, start (restart)\n//\tcreated -> exited   stop\n//\n// A started node also reports its health (health_status: starting or healthy), and a running\n// node reports health changes, like a container with a healthcheck.\nfunc containerTransitionActions(previous, next *trackedContainer) []string {\n\tconst (\n\t\tcreated = clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated\n\t\trunning = clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning\n\t\texited  = clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited\n\t)\n\n\tvar actions []string\n\tpreviousState := \"\"\n\tif previous != nil {\n\t\tpreviousState = previous.state\n\t}\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase previous == nil:\n\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionCreate)\n\t\tswitch next.state {\n\t\tcase running:\n\t\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionStart)\n\t\tcase exited:\n\t\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionStop)\n\t\t}\n\tcase previousState == running && next.state == running && previous.pod != next.pod:\n\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionKill, containerActionStop, containerActionDie,\n\t\t\tcontainerActionStart)\n\tcase previousState == running && next.state != running:\n\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionKill, containerActionStop, containerActionDie)\n\tcase previousState != running && next.state == running:\n\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionStart)\n\tcase previousState == created && next.state == exited:\n\t\tactions = append(actions, containerActionStop)\n\t}\n\n\tif next.state != running {\n\t\treturn actions\n\t}\n\n\tstarted := len(actions) != 0 && actions[len(actions)-1] == containerActionStart\n\tif !started && previous != nil && previous.health == next.health {\n\t\treturn actions\n\t}\n\tif next.health == clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting && !started {\n\t\treturn actions\n\t}\n\n\treturn append(actions, containerActionHealthPrefix+next.health)\n}\n\n// containerRemovalActions are the actions Docker reports when a container is removed: a running\n// one is killed and dies first.\nfunc containerRemovalActions(previous *trackedContainer) []string {\n\tif previous.state == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {\n\t\treturn []string{containerActionKill, containerActionDie, containerActionDestroy}\n\t}\n\n\treturn []string{containerActionDestroy}\n}\n\n// containerActionState is the container state after an action, which every container event\n// reports in its state attribute.\nfunc containerActionState(action, snapshotState string) string {\n\tswitch action {\n\tcase containerActionCreate:\n\t\treturn clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated\n\tcase containerActionStop, containerActionDie, containerActionDestroy:\n\t\treturn clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited\n\tcase containerActionStart, containerActionKill:\n\t\treturn clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning\n\t}\n\tif strings.HasPrefix(action, containerActionHealthPrefix) {\n\t\treturn clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning\n\t}\n\n\treturn snapshotState\n}\n\nfunc (t *containerTracker) emit(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState,\n\tnode clablabruntime.NodeState,\n\taction string,\n\textra map[string]string,\n) {\n\tt.r.sendEvent(ctx, t.sink, c9sContainerEvent(state, node, action, extra))\n}\n\n// c9sContainerEvent is a container event of a node. The actor is the node, as for its interface\n// events; its ID is the container_id inspect reports. Lab and Node let the events command\n// describe the node with the attributes inspect and the Docker runtime report.\nfunc c9sContainerEvent(\n\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState,\n\tnode clablabruntime.NodeState,\n\taction string,\n\textra map[string]string,\n) clablabruntime.Event {\n\tkey := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)\n\tattributes := map[string]string{\n\t\t\"namespace\":                  state.Namespace,\n\t\t\"lab\":                        state.Name,\n\t\t\"node\":                       node.Name,\n\t\tcontainerEventAttributeState: containerActionState(action, node.ContainerState),\n\t}\n\tif node.Pod != \"\" {\n\t\tattributes[\"pod\"] = node.Pod\n\t}\n\tif action == containerActionKill {\n\t\t// Kubernetes stops a pod's containers with SIGTERM.\n\t\tattributes[\"signal\"] = containerEventSignalSIGTERM\n\t}\n\tfor k, v := range extra {\n\t\tattributes[k] = v\n\t}\n\n\tnodeCopy := node\n\n\treturn clablabruntime.Event{\n\t\tTimestamp:   time.Now(),\n\t\tType:        clablabruntime.EventTypeContainer,\n\t\tAction:      action,\n\t\tActorID:     key,\n\t\tActorName:   fmt.Sprintf(\"%s-%s\", state.Name, node.Name),\n\t\tActorFullID: key,\n\t\tAttributes:  attributes,\n\t\tLab:         state,\n\t\tNode:        &nodeCopy,\n\t}\n}",

20: func (r *Runtime) StreamEvents(
21: 	ctx context.Context,
22: 	req clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest,
23: ) (<-chan clablabruntime.Event, <-chan error, error) {
24: 	r, connErr := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
25: 	if connErr != nil {
26: 		return nil, nil, connErr
27: 	}
28: 
29: 	scope, err := r.eventScopeFor(req)
30: 	if err != nil {
31: 		return nil, nil, err
32: 	}
33: 
34: 	events := make(chan clablabruntime.Event, 128)
35: 	errs := make(chan error, 4)
36: 	// changed carries the labs whose Topology, Nodes or pods changed; the container tracker
37: 	// reads them again and reports what changed for their nodes.
38: 	changed := make(chan labRef, 256)
39: 
40: 	go r.trackContainers(ctx, scope, req.IncludeInitialState, changed, events, errs)
41: 
42: 	// Interface state events are always reported, like the netlink-backed events of the local
43: 	// runtimes; statistics only on request. Both come from the same exec per node.
44: 	go r.pollInterfaces(ctx, scope, interfacePollOptions{
45: 		interval:            req.StatsInterval,
46: 		includeStats:        req.IncludeInterfaceStats,
47: 		includeInitialState: req.IncludeInitialState,
48: 	}, events)
49: 
50: 	go r.watchTopologies(ctx, scope, changed, events, errs)
51: 	go r.watchNodes(ctx, scope, changed, errs)
52: 	go r.watchPods(ctx, scope, changed, errs)
53: 
54: 	return events, errs, nil
55: }

274: 			obj, ok := ev.Object.(*unstructured.Unstructured)
275: 			if !ok {
276: 				continue
277: 			}
278: 
279: 			state := stateFromTopology(obj, namespace)
280: 			r.sendEvent(ctx, eventSink, clablabruntime.Event{
281: 				Timestamp: time.Now(),
282: 				Type:      "topology",
283: 				Action:    strings.ToLower(string(ev.Type)),
284: 				ActorID:   fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s", state.Namespace, state.Name),
285: 				ActorName: state.Name,
286: 				Attributes: map[string]string{
287: 					"namespace": state.Namespace,
288: 					"lab":       state.Name,
289: 					"state":     state.State,
290: 					"ready":     fmt.Sprintf("%t", state.Ready),
291: 				},
292: 			})
293: 			sendChangedLab(ctx, changed, labRef{namespace: state.Namespace, lab: state.Name})
294: 		}
295: 	}
296: }
297: 
298: func (r *Runtime) watchPods(
299: 	ctx context.Context,
300: 	scope eventScope,
301: 	changed chan<- labRef,
302: 	errSink chan<- error,
303: ) {
304: 	for {
305: 		watcher, err := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().Pods(scope.namespace).Watch(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{
306: 			LabelSelector: scope.labelSelector(),
307: 		})
308: 		if err != nil {
309: 			if ctx.Err() != nil {
310: 				return
311: 			}
312: 
313: 			sendEventError(ctx, errSink, fmt.Errorf(
314: 				"failed to watch clabernetes pods: %w", err))
315: 			return
316: 		}
317: 
318: 		if !r.forwardPodWatch(ctx, watcher, changed, errSink) {
319: 			return
320: 		}
321: 
322: 		if !sleepContext(ctx, pollInterval) {
323: 			return
324: 		}
325: 	}
326: }
327: 
328: // forwardPodWatch reports the lab of every changed pod to the container tracker.
329: func (r *Runtime) forwardPodWatch(
330: 	ctx context.Context,
331: 	watcher watch.Interface,
332: 	changed chan<- labRef,
333: 	errSink chan<- error,
334: ) bool {
335: 	defer watcher.Stop()
336: 
337: 	for {
338: 		select {
339: 		case <-ctx.Done():
340: 			return false
341: 		case ev, ok := <-watcher.ResultChan():
342: 			if !ok {
343: 				log.Debug("C9s pod watch closed, reconnecting")
344: 				return true
345: 			}
346: 			if ev.Type == watch.Error {
347: 				sendEventError(ctx, errSink, fmt.Errorf(
348: 					"clabernetes pod watch returned an error"))
349: 				return false
350: 			}
351: 
352: 			pod, ok := ev.Object.(*corev1.Pod)
353: 			if !ok {
354: 				continue
355: 			}
356: 
357: 			sendChangedLab(ctx, changed, labRef{
358: 				namespace: pod.Namespace,
359: 				lab:       pod.Labels[labelTopologyOwner],
360: 			})
361: 		}
362: 	}
363: }
364: 
365: func sleepContext(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) bool {
366: 	timer := time.NewTimer(d)
367: 	defer timer.Stop()
368: 
369: 	select {
370: 	case <-timer.C:
371: 		return true
372: 	case <-ctx.Done():
373: 		return false
374: 	}
375: }
376: 
377: func (r *Runtime) sendEvent(
378: 	ctx context.Context,
379: 	eventSink chan<- clablabruntime.Event,
380: 	event clablabruntime.Event,
381: ) {
382: 	select {
383: 	case eventSink <- event:
384: 	case <-ctx.Done():
385: 	}
386: }
387: 
388: func sendEventError(ctx context.Context, errSink chan<- error, err error) {
389: 	select {
390: 	case errSink <- err:
391: 	case <-ctx.Done():
392: 	}
393: }

149: // newestPod prefers a pod that is not being deleted, then a running pod and, among equals, the
150: // newest one: several pods can match a node during a rolling update or a restart, when the old
151: // pod terminates while its replacement starts.
152: func newestPod(current, candidate *corev1.Pod) *corev1.Pod {
153: 	if current == nil {
154: 		return candidate
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	currentDeleting := current.DeletionTimestamp != nil
158: 	candidateDeleting := candidate.DeletionTimestamp != nil
159: 	if currentDeleting != candidateDeleting {
160: 		if candidateDeleting {
161: 			return current
162: 		}
163: 
164: 		return candidate
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	currentRunning := current.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
168: 	candidateRunning := candidate.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
169: 	if currentRunning != candidateRunning {
170: 		if candidateRunning {
171: 			return candidate
172: 		}
173: 
174: 		return current
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	if candidate.CreationTimestamp.After(current.CreationTimestamp.Time) {
178: 		return candidate
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	return current
182: }

249: 			); condition != nil &&

251: 				node.State = "stopped"
252: 			}
253: 			node.Ready = false
254: 		} else if pod := podsByNode[primary]; node.State == "" && pod != nil &&
255: 			pod.Status.Phase != "" {
256: 			node.State = strings.ToLower(string(pod.Status.Phase))
257: 		}
258: 		node.ContainerState = nodeContainerState(stopRequested, podsByNode[primary])
259: 		if node.ContainerState == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {
260: 			node.Health = nodeHealth(node, resourcesByName[nodeName])
261: 		}
262: 		nodesByName[nodeName] = node
263: 	}
264: 
265: 	// Nodes grouped through network-mode container: share the pod of the group's primary
266: 	// node. Before the controller observed the device containers, the pod's default-container
267: 	// annotation names the primary node's container.
268: 	for nodeName, node := range nodesByName {
269: 		primary := resolvePrimaryNode(nodeName, networkModes)
270: 		pod := podsByNode[primary]
271: 		if pod == nil {
272: 			continue
273: 		}
274: 
275: 		node.Pod = pod.Name
276: 		if node.Container == "" && primary == nodeName {
277: 			node.Container = pod.Annotations[defaultContainerAnnotation]
278: 		}
279: 		nodesByName[nodeName] = node
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(nodesByName))
283: 	for nodeName := range nodesByName {
284: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
285: 	}
286: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
287: 
288: 	state.Nodes = make([]clablabruntime.NodeState, 0, len(nodeNames))
289: 	allReady := len(nodeNames) > 0 // codespell:ignore allready
290: 	allStopped := len(nodeNames) > 0
291: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
292: 		node := nodesByName[nodeName]
293: 		state.Nodes = append(state.Nodes, node)
294: 		allReady = allReady && node.Ready // codespell:ignore allready
295: 		allStopped = allStopped && node.State == "stopped"
296: 	}
297: 
298: 	switch {
299: 	case allReady: // codespell:ignore allready
300: 		state.State = "running"
301: 		state.Ready = true
302: 	case allStopped:
303: 		state.State = "stopped"
304: 		state.Ready = false
305: 	case len(nodeNames) != 0:
306: 		state.State = "partial"
307: 		state.Ready = false
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	return nil
311: }
312: 
313: // nodeContainerState is the state of a node in container runtime terms, from its pod: created
314: // while the pod is scheduled and prepared (init containers), running once the device containers
315: // run, and exited once the node was stopped, its pod is being deleted, or the pod ended. Between
316: // the pods of a restart the node is exited, then created.
317: func nodeContainerState(stopRequested bool, pod *corev1.Pod) string {
318: 	switch {
319: 	case pod == nil && stopRequested:
320: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
321: 	case pod == nil:
322: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
323: 	case stopRequested || pod.DeletionTimestamp != nil:
324: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
325: 	}
326: 
327: 	switch pod.Status.Phase {
328: 	case corev1.PodRunning:
329: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
330: 	case corev1.PodSucceeded, corev1.PodFailed:
331: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
332: 	default:
333: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
334: 	}
335: }
336: 
337: // nodeHealth is the health of a running node: healthy once the Node is ready or its device
338: // containers are, starting before. Device containers are the analogue of a container
339: // healthcheck: a node whose links wait for a stopped peer is not ready, but its device is.
340: func nodeHealth(node clablabruntime.NodeState, resource *unstructured.Unstructured) string {
341: 	if node.Ready {
342: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy
343: 	}
344: 	if resource != nil {
345: 		if condition := nodeCondition(resource, nodeConditionContainersReady); condition != nil &&
346: 			condition.status == string(metav1.ConditionTrue) {
347: 			return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy
348: 		}
349: 	}
350: 
351: 	return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting
352: }

54: func (r *netlinkRegistry) Start(container *clabruntime.GenericContainer) {
55: 	clone := cloneContainer(container)
56: 	if clone == nil {
57: 		return
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	id := clone.ID
61: 	if id == "" {
62: 		id = clone.ShortID
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	if id == "" {
66: 		return
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	r.mu.Lock()
70: 	if _, exists := r.watchers[id]; exists {
71: 		r.mu.Unlock()
72: 
73: 		return
74: 	}
75: 
76: 	watcherCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(r.ctx)
77: 	watcher := &netlinkWatcher{
78: 		container:       clone,

84: 	}

126: 	runtime clabruntime.ContainerRuntime,
127: 	ev clabruntime.ContainerEvent,

130: 		return

259: func (w *netlinkWatcher) run(ctx context.Context, registry *netlinkRegistry) {

271: 		return

274: 	// The states outlive a subscription, so a resubscribe only reports what
275: 	// changed while no subscription was active.
276: 	states := make(map[int]ifaceSnapshot)

278: 	var statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample
279: 	if w.includeStats {

281: 	}

283: 	initial := true
284: 	failures := 0
285: 	delay := watchRetryDelay
286: 
287: 	for {
288: 		subscribed, err := w.watch(ctx, registry, states, statsSamples, initial)
289: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
290: 			return
291: 		}
292: 
293: 		if subscribed {
294: 			initial = false
295: 			failures = 0
296: 			delay = watchRetryDelay
297: 
298: 			log.Warnf(
299: 				"netlink subscription for container %s ended, resubscribing: %v",
300: 				containerName,
301: 				err,
302: 			)
303: 		} else {
304: 			failures++
305: 			if failures >= watchMaxAttempts {
306: 				log.Warnf("stopped watching interfaces of container %s: %v", containerName, err)
307: 
308: 				return
309: 			}
310: 
311: 			log.Debugf(
312: 				"failed to watch interfaces of container %s, retrying in %s: %v",
313: 				containerName,
314: 				delay,
315: 				err,
316: 			)
317: 		}
318: 
319: 		select {
320: 		case <-time.After(delay):
321: 		case <-ctx.Done():
322: 			return
323: 		}
324: 
325: 		delay = min(delay*2, watchMaxRetryDelay)
326: 	}

330: // them until ctx ends or the subscription fails. It reports whether it

332: // between listing and subscribing is lost.

347: 		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to open netns: %w", err)

388: 		},

459: // processExisting records a link listed when the subscription started. On the
460: // first subscription a new link is reported as a snapshot when requested; after
461: // a resubscribe it is reported as created.
462: //
463: // The listing can be older than the check in removeVanishedLinks, so it can
464: // still hold a link that check reported as deleted. Such a link is skipped; its
465: // deletion notification follows and is ignored, as the link is not tracked.
466: func (w *netlinkWatcher) processExisting(
467: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
468: 	statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample,
469: 	link netlink.Link,
470: 	netemInfos map[int]netemInfo,
471: 	vanished map[int]struct{},
472: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
473: 	initial bool,
474: ) {
475: 	if link == nil || link.Attrs() == nil {
476: 		return
477: 	}
478: 
479: 	if _, ok := vanished[link.Attrs().Index]; ok {
480: 		return
481: 	}
482: 
483: 	snapshot := withNetem(snapshotFromLink(link), netemInfos)
484: 	previous, exists := states[snapshot.Index]
485: 
486: 	if exists && snapshot.equal(previous) {
487: 		return
488: 	}
489: 
490: 	states[snapshot.Index] = snapshot
491: 	if statsSamples != nil {
492: 		if sample, ok := newStatsSample(snapshot, time.Now()); ok {
493: 			statsSamples[snapshot.Index] = sample
494: 		}
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	switch {
498: 	case exists:
499: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "update", snapshot)
500: 	case !initial:
501: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "create", snapshot)
502: 	case w.includeSnapshot:
503: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "snapshot", snapshot)
504: 	}
505: }

507: // removeVanishedLinks reports the links that were deleted while no
508: // subscription was active and returns their indexes.
509: func (w *netlinkWatcher) removeVanishedLinks(
510: 	netHandle *netlink.Handle,
511: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
512: 	statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample,
513: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
514: ) map[int]struct{} {
515: 	current, err := snapshotInterfaces(netHandle)
516: 	if err != nil {
517: 		log.Debugf(
518: 			"failed to list interfaces of container %s: %v",
519: 			firstContainerName(w.container),
520: 			err,
521: 		)
522: 
523: 		return nil
524: 	}
525: 
526: 	vanished := map[int]struct{}{}
527: 
528: 	for idx, snapshot := range states {
529: 		if _, ok := current[idx]; ok {
530: 			continue
531: 		}
532: 
533: 		vanished[idx] = struct{}{}
534: 
535: 		delete(states, idx)
536: 		delete(statsSamples, idx)
537: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "delete", snapshot)
538: 	}
539: 
540: 	return vanished
541: }

51: // Identity is the Kubernetes identity a lab runtime acts as, through user impersonation. The

526: // is not an error); the output is a valid capture whenever it stops.

closing it stops resizing.\n388: \tResize <-chan TerminalSize\n389: }\n390: \n391: // CommandExitError reports a command that ran and exited with a nonzero code.\n392: type CommandExitError struct {\n393: \tCode int\n394: }\n395: \n396: func (e *CommandExitError) Error() string {\n397: \treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"command exited with code %d\", e.Code)\n398: }\n399: \n400: // LogRequest selects the node log StreamLogs writes.\n401: type LogRequest struct {\n402: \t// Name is the lab name.\n403: \tName      string\n404: \tNamespace string\n405: \t// NodeName is the node whose log is streamed, as the topology or the runtime names it.\n406: \tNodeName string\n407: \t// Container overrides the node's primary device container.\n408: \tContainer string\n409: \t// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; It returns an error wrapping\n542: // ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource metrics.\n543: type NodeStatsSampler interface {\n544: \tSampleStats(ctx context.Context, req InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)\n545: }\n546: \n547: type LabRuntime interface {\n548: \tDeploy(context.Context, DeployRequest) (*LabState, error)\n549: \tDestroy(context.Context, DestroyRequest) error\n550: \tInspect(context.Context, InspectRequest) (*LabState, error)\n551: \tList(context.Context, ListRequest) ([]*LabState, error)\n552: \tExec(context.Context, ExecRequest) (*clabexec.ExecResult, error)\n553: \tStart(context.Context, NodeRequest) error\n554: \tStop(context.Context, NodeRequest) error\n555: \tRestart(context.Context, NodeRequest) error\n556: \tSave(context.Context, SaveRequest) (*SaveResult, error)\n557: \tStreamEvents(context.Context, EventStreamRequest) (<-chan Event, <-chan error, error)\n558: }\n559: \n560: // LabExistenceChecker lets controller-driven runtimes report whether a lab has remote state.\n561: // Core uses it to distinguish a fresh deployment from reconciliation without consulting the\n562: // local container runtime.\n563: type LabExistenceChecker interface {\n564: \tLabExists(context.Context, InspectRequest) (bool, error)\n565: }\n566: \n567: // TopologyValidator validates the runtime-specific topology subset without changing remote state.\n568: type TopologyValidator interface {\n569: \tValidate(context.Context, DeployRequest) error\n570: }\n571: \n572: // TopologyPlanner compiles and diffs a desired topology without changing remote state.\n573: type TopologyPlanner interface {\n574: \tPlan(context.Context, DeployRequest) (*DeployPlan, error)\n575: }\n576: \n577: // Manifest is one remote resource a lab runtime would create for a topology, ready to be\n578: // serialized and applied by hand. Object is the complete resource including its type and\n579: // metadata; the identity fields are duplicated for summaries and tests.\n580: type Manifest struct {\n581: \tAPIVersion string\n582: \tKind       string\n583: \tNamespace  string\n584: \tName       string\n585: \tObject     map[string]any\n586: }\n587: \n588: // ManifestEmitter renders the exact resources a lab runtime would create for a topology, in\n589: // apply order, without reading or changing remote state.\n590: type ManifestEmitter interface {\n591: \tManifests(context.Context, DeployRequest) ([]Manifest, error)\n592: }\n593: \n594: type Initializer func(Config) (LabRuntime, error)\n595: \n596: var LabRuntimes = map[string]Initializer{}\n597: \n598: func Register(name string, init Initializer) {\n599: \tLabRuntimes[name] = init\n600: }\n601: \n602: func IsLabRuntimeName(name string) bool {\n603: \t_, ok := LabRuntimes[strings.ToLower(name)]\n604: \treturn ok\n605: }\n606: \n607: func Init(name string, cfg Config) (LabRuntime, error) {\n608: \tname = strings.ToLower(name)\n609: \tinit, ok := LabRuntimes[name]\n610: \tif !ok {\n611: \t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"unknown lab runtime %q\", name)\n612: \t}\n613: \n614: \treturn init(cfg)\n615: }\n\n(End of file - total 615 lines)\n</content>",

A server that\n// runs labs for many users sets it per call, so the cluster's RBAC and audit log see the user.\ntype Identity struct {\n\tUser   string\n\tGroups []string\n}\n\n// IsZero reports whether the identity leaves the configured credentials as they are.\nfunc (i Identity) IsZero() bool {\n\treturn i.User == \"\" && len(i.Groups) == 0\n}\n\n// Equal reports whether two identities impersonate the same user and groups.\nfunc (i Identity) Equal(other Identity) bool {\n\treturn i.User == other.User && slices.Equal(i.Groups, other.Groups)\n}\n\ntype Config struct {\n\tTimeout   time.Duration\n\tNamespace string\n\t// Identity is the identity of every call that does not set its own.\n\tIdentity Identity\n\n\t// KindLinkApplyMode resolves the default link apply mode (\"live\", \"restart\" or\n\t// \"recreate\") a node kind declares, as containerlab's node registry reports it. An\n\t// empty result means the kind is unknown and the conservative recreate default\n\t// applies. Lab runtimes use it to predict the node lifecycle impact of link changes.\n\tKindLinkApplyMode func(kind string) string\n}\n\ntype DeployRequest struct {\n\tName               string\n\tNamespace          string\n\tOwner              string\n\tTopologyFile       string\n\tTopologyLabDir     string\n\tTopologyDefinition []byte\n\tWait               bool\n\tTimeout            time.Duration\n\t// MaxWorkers limits concurrent independent operations performed by the runtime.\n\tMaxWorkers uint\n\t// NoTopologyCR deploys without a controller-owned topology object: the runtime compiles the\n\t// topology client-side and manages the individual lab resources directly.\n\tNoTopologyCR bool\n\t// ImagePullSecret names the same-namespace Docker-config Secret placed on device pods\n\t// through Pod.spec.imagePullSecrets. Empty means the lab references no pull secret at\n\t// all: public images and clusters whose runtime already holds credentials need none.\n\tImagePullSecret string\n\t// ExposeType controls the Kubernetes Service type c9s creates for lab nodes. Empty uses the\n\t// c9s CRD default.\n\tExposeType string\n\t// NoPersistence deploys the lab on ephemeral node storage. Name limits the stream to one\n// lab, in its namespace. Empty means Name.\n\tTopologyName string\n\tKind         string\n\tImage        string\n\t// Type and Group are the node's type and group when the topology set them.\n\tType  string\n\tGroup string\n\t// State is the runtime's own view of the node, such as the clabernetes Node readiness, or\n\t// stopped.\n\tState string\n\tReady bool\n\t// ContainerState is the node's state in container runtime terms: created, running or\n\t// exited (the ContainerState* constants). Empty when the node does not run.\n\tHealth string\n\t// MgmtIPv4Address and MgmtIPv6Address are the node's allocated management addresses in\n\t// CIDR notation, when the runtime reports them.\n\tMgmtIPv4Address     string\n\tMgmtIPv6Address     string\n\tLoadBalancerAddress string\n\t// Pod is the pod that runs the node. Nodes that share a network namespace share a pod.\n\tPod string\n\t// Container is the node's primary device container in Pod.\n\tContainer string\n\t// NodeUID identifies the runtime's node resource (the clabernetes Node UID).\n\tNodeUID string\n\t// ExposedPorts are the node ports the runtime publishes through a Service.\n\tExposedPorts []ExposedPort\n}\n\n// ExposedPort is a node port a lab runtime publishes through a Service.\ntype ExposedPort = clabtypes.ExposedPort\n\ntype LabState struct {\n\tName      string\n\tNamespace string\n\tOwner     string\n\t// TopologyPath is the absolute path of the topology file the lab was deployed from, on the\n\t// machine that deployed it. It is not a Kubernetes action; it communicates the\n\t// lifecycle impact of an apply.\n\tChangeRecreate ChangeAction = \"recreate\"\n)\n\ntype ResourceChange struct {\n\tAction    ChangeAction `json:\"action\"`\n\tKind      string       `json:\"kind\"`\n\tNamespace string       `json:\"namespace,omitempty\"`\n\tName      string       `json:\"name\"`\n}\n\n// DeployPlan describes the remote resources a lab runtime would change without mutating them.\ntype DeployPlan struct {\n\tLabName   string           `json:\"lab-name\"`\n\tNamespace string           `json:\"namespace\"`\n\tChanges   []ResourceChange `json:\"changes\"`\n}\n\ntype Event struct {\n\tTimestamp   time.Time\n\tType        string\n\tAction      string\n\tActorID     string\n\tActorName   string\n\tActorFullID string\n\t// Attributes are the runtime's own attributes. Event consumers add the attributes the\n\t// container runtimes report from Lab, Node and Interface.\n\tAttributes map[string]string\n\t// Lab and Node are the lab node a container or interface event is about, as Inspect\n\t// reports it. containerlab's events command describes the node from them the same way\n\t// inspect does, so both agree and match what the container runtimes report.\n\tLab  *LabState\n\tNode *NodeState\n\t// Interface is the interface an interface event reports.\n\tInterface *InterfaceEventData\n}\n\n// Event types and the origin attribute of lab runtime events.\nconst (\n\tEventTypeContainer = \"container\"\n\tEventTypeInterface = \"interface\"\n\t// EventOriginSnapshot marks the events of --initial-state, in the origin attribute.\n\tEventOriginSnapshot = \"snapshot\"\n)\n\n// InterfaceEventData describes an interface of a node the way the container runtimes' interface\n// events do (netlink).\ntype InterfaceEventData struct {\n\t// Name is the interface name inside the node.\n\tName string\n\t// Alias is the name the topology gave the interface when the node kind maps it (for\n\t// example ethernet-1/1 for SR Linux e1-1).\n\tAlias string\n\tIndex int\n\tMTU   int\n\tMAC   string\n\t// OperState is the operational state in netlink's vocabulary: up, down, lower-layer-down,\n\t// dormant, testing, not-present or unknown.\n\tOperState string\n\t// Type is the link type in netlink's vocabulary, such as veth or device (loopback).\n\tType string\n\t// Stats are set on stats events.\n\tStats *InterfaceStats\n}\n\n// InterfaceStats are the counters and rates of an interface stats event.\ntype InterfaceStats struct {\n\tRxBytes   uint64\n\tTxBytes   uint64\n\tRxPackets uint64\n\tTxPackets uint64\n\tRxBps     float64\n\tTxBps     float64\n\tRxPps     float64\n\tTxPps     float64\n\tInterval  time.Duration\n}\n\n// NodeLocation is the workload that runs a lab node.\ntype NodeLocation struct {\n\t// NodeName is the node name the runtime carries (the sanitized name).\n\tNodeName  string\n\tNamespace string\n\tPod       string\n\t// Container is the node's primary device container in Pod.\n\tContainer string\n\t// NodeUID identifies the runtime's node resource (the clabernetes Node UID).\n\tNodeUID string\n\t// ExposedPorts are the node ports the runtime publishes through a Service.\n\tExposedPorts        []ExposedPort\n\tLoadBalancerAddress string\n}\n\n// TerminalSize is the size of an interactive terminal, in characters.\ntype TerminalSize struct {\n\tWidth  uint16\n\tHeight uint16\n}\n\n// AttachRequest selects the node and the command of an interactive session.\ntype AttachRequest struct {\n\t// Name is the lab name.\n\tName      string\n\tNamespace string\n\t// NodeName is the node to attach to, as the topology or the runtime names it.\n\tNodeName string\n\t// Container overrides the node's primary device container.\n\tContainer string\n\t// Command runs in the container; empty runs \"sh\".\n\tCommand []string\n\t// TTY allocates a terminal. Stdout then carries the combined output, and Resize applies.\n\tTTY      bool\n\tIdentity Identity\n}\n\n// AttachStreams connects an interactive session. Nil streams are not attached.\ntype AttachStreams struct {\n\tStdin  io.Reader\n\tStdout io.Writer\n\tStderr io.Writer\n\t// Resize delivers terminal size changes of a TTY session; closing it stops resizing.\n\tResize <-chan TerminalSize\n}\n\n// CommandExitError reports a command that ran and exited with a nonzero code.\ntype CommandExitError struct {\n\tCode int\n}\n\nfunc (e *CommandExitError) Error() string {\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"command exited with code %d\", e.Code)\n}\n\n// LogRequest selects the node log StreamLogs writes.\ntype LogRequest struct {\n\t// Name is the lab name.\n\tName      string\n\tNamespace string\n\t// NodeName is the node whose log is streamed, as the topology or the runtime names it.\n\tNodeName string\n\t// Container overrides the node's primary device container.\n\tContainer string\n\t// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.\n\tTail *int64\n\t// Follow keeps streaming new log lines until the context ends.\n\tFollow bool\n\t// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.\n\tTimestamps bool\n\tIdentity   Identity\n}\n\n// NodeStats is a resource usage sample of a node.\ntype NodeStats struct {\n\tNodeName  string\n\tNamespace string\n\tPod       string\n\t// CPUMilliCores is the CPU usage of the node's device containers, in thousandths of a core.\n\tCPUMilliCores int64\n\t// MemoryBytes is the memory working set of the node's device containers.\n\tMemoryBytes int64\n\t// Timestamp and Window describe the sampling interval the usage was measured over.\n\tTimestamp time.Time\n\tWindow    time.Duration\n}\n\n// ErrMetricsUnavailable reports a cluster without a resource metrics API (metrics.k8s.io), for\n// example one without metrics-server.\nvar ErrMetricsUnavailable = errors.New(\"metrics API (metrics.k8s.io) not available\")\n\n// ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion reports a cluster whose controller release lacks the contract a\n// lab runtime needs. It returns\n// an error wrapping ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion when the release is too old.\ntype SupportChecker interface {\n\tCheckSupport(ctx context.Context, identity Identity) error\n}\n\n// NodeLocator resolves lab nodes to the workloads that run them. Empty NodeRequest.Nodes\n// locates every node of the lab.\ntype NodeLocator interface {\n\tLocateNode(ctx context.Context, req NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)\n}\n\n// NodeAttacher runs an interactive command (stdin, TTY and resize) in a node's container. It\n// returns a *CommandExitError when the command exits with a nonzero code.\ntype NodeAttacher interface {\n\tAttach(ctx context.Context, req AttachRequest, streams AttachStreams) error\n}\n\n// NodeLogStreamer writes a node container's log.\ntype NodeLogStreamer interface {\n\tStreamLogs(ctx context.Context, req LogRequest, w io.Writer) error\n}\n\n// NodePortForwarder opens a stream to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs). It\n// returns when Duration passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or the context ended (which\n// is not an error); the output is a valid capture whenever it stops.\ntype PacketCapturer interface {\n\tCaptureInterfaces(ctx context.Context, req NodeRequest) ([]CaptureInterface, error)\n\tCapture(ctx context.Context, req CaptureRequest, w io.Writer) error\n}\n\n// InterfaceInspector lists the link interfaces of a lab's nodes with their current state, in the\n// shape of `inspect interfaces`.\ntype InterfaceInspector interface {\n\tInspectInterfaces(\n\t\tctx context.Context,\n\t\treq NodeRequest,\n\t) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error)\n}\n\n// NodeStatsSampler reports the resource usage of a lab's nodes. Object is the complete resource including its type and\n// metadata; the identity fields are duplicated for summaries and tests.\ntype Manifest struct {\n\tAPIVersion string\n\tKind       string\n\tNamespace  string\n\tName       string\n\tObject     map[string]any\n}\n\n// ManifestEmitter renders the exact resources a lab runtime would create for a topology, in\n// apply order, without reading or changing remote state.\ntype ManifestEmitter interface {\n\tManifests(context.Context, DeployRequest) ([]Manifest, error)\n}\n\ntype Initializer func(Config) (LabRuntime, error)\n\nvar LabRuntimes = map[string]Initializer{}\n\nfunc Register(name string, init Initializer) {\n\tLabRuntimes[name] = init\n}\n\nfunc IsLabRuntimeName(name string) bool {\n\t_, ok := LabRuntimes[strings.ToLower(name)]\n\treturn ok\n}\n\nfunc Init(name string, cfg Config) (LabRuntime, error) {\n\tname = strings.ToLower(name)\n\tinit, ok := LabRuntimes[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"unknown lab runtime %q\", name)\n\t}\n\n\treturn init(cfg)\n}",

98: 	captureReorderWindow time.Duration
99: 	// support checks once per runtime instance, before the first cluster call, that the
100: 	// cluster runs a clabernetes release with the contract this runtime needs. Every view
101: 	// shares it. It is nil when the clients were injected (tests).
102: 	support *supportCheck
103: }
104: 
105: // kubeClients is the set of Kubernetes clients a runtime view operates with.
106: type kubeClients struct {
107: 	dynamic    dynamic.Interface
108: 	kube       kubernetes.Interface
109: 	restConfig *rest.Config
110: }
111: 
112: // clientLoader loads the kubeconfig once and builds, and caches, the Kubernetes clients of
113: // every identity from it.
114: type clientLoader struct {
115: 	loadConfig func() (*rest.Config, string, error)
116: 	newClients func(*rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error)
117: 
118: 	once      sync.Once
119: 	base      *rest.Config
120: 	namespace string
121: 	err       error
122: 
123: 	mu         sync.Mutex
124: 	byIdentity map[string]*kubeClients
125: }
126: 
127: func newClientLoader() *clientLoader {
128: 	return &clientLoader{
129: 		loadConfig: kubeClientConfig,
130: 		newClients: newKubeClients,
131: 	}
132: }
133: 
134: func newKubeClients(restConfig *rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error) {
135: 	client, err := dynamic.NewForConfig(restConfig)
136: 	if err != nil {
137: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes dynamic client: %w", err)
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	kubeClient, err := kubernetes.NewForConfig(restConfig)
141: 	if err != nil {
142: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes client: %w", err)
143: 	}
144: 
145: 	return &kubeClients{dynamic: client, kube: kubeClient, restConfig: restConfig}, nil
146: }
147: 
148: // load returns the clients of an identity. The impersonation is part of the rest config, so it
149: // applies to every transport built from it: REST calls, watches, log streams, and the SPDY and
150: // websocket upgrades of exec, attach and port-forward.
151: func (l *clientLoader) load(
152: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
153: ) (*kubeClients, string, error) {
154: 	l.once.Do(func() {
155: 		l.base, l.namespace, l.err = l.loadConfig()
156: 		if l.namespace == "" {
157: 			l.namespace = defaultNamespace
158: 		}
159: 	})
160: 	if l.err != nil {
161: 		return nil, "", l.err
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	key := identityKey(identity)
165: 
166: 	l.mu.Lock()
167: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
168: 
169: 	if clients, ok := l.byIdentity[key]; ok {
170: 		return clients, l.namespace, nil
171: 	}
172: 
173: 	restConfig := rest.CopyConfig(l.base)
174: 	if !identity.IsZero() {
175: 		restConfig.Impersonate = rest.ImpersonationConfig{
176: 			UserName: identity.User,
177: 			Groups:   slices.Clone(identity.Groups),
178: 		}
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	clients, err := l.newClients(restConfig)
182: 	if err != nil {
183: 		return nil, "", err
184: 	}
185: 	if l.byIdentity == nil {
186: 		l.byIdentity = map[string]*kubeClients{}
187: 	}
188: 	l.byIdentity[key] = clients
189: 
190: 	return clients, l.namespace, nil
191: }
192: 
193: func identityKey(identity clablabruntime.Identity) string {
194: 	return identity.User + "\x00" + strings.Join(identity.Groups, "\x00")
195: }
196: 
197: // connect returns a view of the runtime with the Kubernetes clients of an identity populated,
198: // loading the kubeconfig on first use. A zero identity uses the runtime's configured identity.
199: // Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first, so it also runs the
200: // clabernetes version check once per runtime instance, before the first cluster call.
201: func (r *Runtime) connect(
202: 	ctx context.Context,
203: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
204: ) (*Runtime, error) {
205: 	if identity.IsZero() {
206: 		identity = r.identity
207: 	}
208: 	if r.connected && identity.Equal(r.identity) {
209: 		return r, nil
210: 	}
211: 	if r.clients == nil {
212: 		// clients were injected (tests); they act as the identity they were built with
213: 		if err := r.support.ensure(ctx, r); err != nil {
214: 			return nil, err
215: 		}
216: 
217: 		return r, nil
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	clients, namespace, err := r.clients.load(identity)
221: 	if err != nil {
222: 		return nil, err
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	view := *r
226: 	view.client = clients.dynamic
227: 	view.kubeClient = clients.kube
228: 	view.restConfig = clients.restConfig
229: 	if view.namespace == "" {
230: 		view.namespace = namespace
231: 	}
232: 	view.identity = identity
233: 	view.connected = true
234: 
235: 	if err := r.support.ensure(ctx, &view); err != nil {
236: 		return nil, err
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	return &view, nil
240: }
241: 
242: func withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
243: 	verbosity := -1
244: 	if log.GetLevel() <= log.DebugLevel {
245: 		verbosity = 3
246: 	}
247: 	logger := funcr.New(func(prefix, args string) {
248: 		log.Debug("Kubernetes client", "log", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+" "+args))
249: 	}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})
250: 
251: 	return klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)
252: }
253: 
254: func init() {
255: 	clablabruntime.Register(clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName, New)
256: }
257: 
258: // New returns the c9s lab runtime. It does not load the kubeconfig: the Kubernetes clients
259: // are created on the first operation that needs the cluster.
260: func New(cfg clablabruntime.Config) (clablabruntime.LabRuntime, error) {
261: 	return &Runtime{
262: 		labNamespaceOverride: configuredLabNamespace(cfg.Namespace),
263: 		timeout:              cfg.Timeout,
264: 		kindLinkApplyMode:    cfg.KindLinkApplyMode,
265: 		identity:             cfg.Identity,
266: 		clients:              newClientLoader(),
267: 		support:              &supportCheck{},
268: 		captureSegment:       captureSegmentFromEnv(),
269: 		captureReorderWindow: captureReorderWindowFromEnv(),
270: 	}, nil
271: }

The impersonation is part of the rest config, so it\n// applies to every transport built from it: REST calls, watches, log streams, and the SPDY and\n// websocket upgrades of exec, attach and port-forward.\nfunc (l *clientLoader) load(\n\tidentity clablabruntime.Identity,\n) (*kubeClients, string, error) {\n\tl.once.Do(func() {\n\t\tl.base, l.namespace, l.err = l.loadConfig()\n\t\tif l.namespace == \"\" {\n\t\t\tl.namespace = defaultNamespace\n\t\t}\n\t})\n\tif l.err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, \"\", l.err\n\t}\n\n\tkey := identityKey(identity)\n\n\tl.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer l.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tif clients, ok := l.byIdentity[key]; ok {\n\t\treturn clients, l.namespace, nil\n\t}\n\n\trestConfig := rest.CopyConfig(l.base)\n\tif !identity.IsZero() {\n\t\trestConfig.Impersonate = rest.ImpersonationConfig{\n\t\t\tUserName: identity.User,\n\t\t\tGroups:   slices.Clone(identity.Groups),\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tclients, err := l.newClients(restConfig)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, \"\", err\n\t}\n\tif l.byIdentity == nil {\n\t\tl.byIdentity = map[string]*kubeClients{}\n\t}\n\tl.byIdentity[key] = clients\n\n\treturn clients, l.namespace, nil\n}\n\nfunc identityKey(identity clablabruntime.Identity) string {\n\treturn identity.User + \"\\x00\" + strings.Join(identity.Groups, \"\\x00\")\n}\n\n// connect returns a view of the runtime with the Kubernetes clients of an identity populated,\n// loading the kubeconfig on first use. A zero identity uses the runtime's configured identity.\n// Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first, so it also runs the\n// clabernetes version check once per runtime instance, before the first cluster call.\nfunc (r *Runtime) connect(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tidentity clablabruntime.Identity,\n) (*Runtime, error) {\n\tif identity.IsZero() {\n\t\tidentity = r.identity\n\t}\n\tif r.connected && identity.Equal(r.identity) {\n\t\treturn r, nil\n\t}\n\tif r.clients == nil {\n\t\t// clients were injected (tests); they act as the identity they were built with\n\t\tif err := r.support.ensure(ctx, r); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn r, nil\n\t}\n\n\tclients, namespace, err := r.clients.load(identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tview := *r\n\tview.client = clients.dynamic\n\tview.kubeClient = clients.kube\n\tview.restConfig = clients.restConfig\n\tif view.namespace == \"\" {\n\t\tview.namespace = namespace\n\t}\n\tview.identity = identity\n\tview.connected = true\n\n\tif err := r.support.ensure(ctx, &view); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn &view, nil\n}\n\nfunc withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx context.Context) context.Context {\n\tverbosity := -1\n\tif log.GetLevel() <= log.DebugLevel {\n\t\tverbosity = 3\n\t}\n\tlogger := funcr.New(func(prefix, args string) {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Kubernetes client\", \"log\", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+\" \"+args))\n\t}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})\n\n\treturn klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)\n}\n\nfunc init() {\n\tclablabruntime.Register(clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName, New)\n}\n\n// New returns the c9s lab runtime. It does not load the kubeconfig: the Kubernetes clients\n// are created on the first operation that needs the cluster.\nfunc New(cfg clablabruntime.Config) (clablabruntime.LabRuntime, error) {\n\treturn &Runtime{\n\t\tlabNamespaceOverride: configuredLabNamespace(cfg.Namespace),\n\t\ttimeout:              cfg.Timeout,\n\t\tkindLinkApplyMode:    cfg.KindLinkApplyMode,\n\t\tidentity:             cfg.Identity,\n\t\tclients:              newClientLoader(),\n\t\tsupport:              &supportCheck{},\n\t\tcaptureSegment:       captureSegmentFromEnv(),\n\t\tcaptureReorderWindow: captureReorderWindowFromEnv(),\n\t}, nil\n}",

189: 				link.ActorID != "c9s-lab1/lab1/r1" ||

191: 				link.ActorName != "lab1-r1" || link.Interface.Alias != tt.alias ||

273: 		sink,

275: 	links := []clabwireInterface{{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1", Alias: "ethernet-1/1"}}
276: 	start := time.Now()
277: 	first := interfaceTestSample("r1", start, links, podInterfaces("e1-1", "up"))
278: 	second := interfaceTestSample("r1", start.Add(time.Second), links, podInterfaces("e1-1", "up"))
279: 	for idx := range second.stats {
280: 		second.stats[idx].RxBytes = first.stats[idx].RxBytes + 1000
281: 	}
282: 
283: 	p.processSample(context.Background(), first)
284: 	_ = drain(sink)
285: 	p.processSample(context.Background(), second)
286: 	got := interfacesByName(drain(sink))
287: 	if len(got) != 3 {
288: 		t.Fatalf("stats reported for %v, want e1-1, eth0 and lo", got)
289: 	}
290: 	stats := got["e1-1"]
291: 	if stats.Action != interfaceActionStats || stats.Interface.Alias != "ethernet-1/1" ||
292: 		stats.Interface.Index != 7 || stats.Interface.OperState != "up" ||
293: 		stats.Interface.Stats == nil || stats.Interface.Stats.RxBps != 8000 ||
294: 		stats.Interface.Stats.Interval != time.Second {
295: 		t.Fatalf("e1-1 stats = %+v %+v", stats, stats.Interface)
296: 	}
297: }

299: // listingExec answers clabwire --list-interfaces with the listing of the pod and counts the
300: // listings.
301: type listingExec struct {
302: 	mu       sync.Mutex
303: 	listings map[string][]clabwireInterface
304: 	calls    int
305: }
306: 
307: func (l *listingExec) exec(
308: 	_ context.Context,
309: 	_, pod, container string,
310: 	command []string,
311: 	_ io.Reader,
312: 	stdout, _ io.Writer,
313: ) error {
314: 	l.mu.Lock()
315: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
316: 
317: 	if container != clabwireContainer || !slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
318: 		return nil
319: 	}
320: 	l.calls++
321: 
322: 	return json.NewEncoder(stdout).Encode(l.listings[pod])
323: }

325: func TestInterfacePollerListsAPodOncePerInterfaceSet(t *testing.T) {
326: 	t.Parallel()
327: 
328: 	listing := &listingExec{listings: map[string][]clabwireInterface{
329: 		"lab1-r1-abc": {
330: 			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1", Alias: "ethernet-1/1"},
331: 			{Node: "r1b", Interface: "e1-2"},
332: 		},
333: 	}}
334: 	r := &Runtime{podExec: listing.exec}
335: 	p := newInterfacePoller(
336: 		r,
337: 		eventScope{},
338: 		interfacePollOptions{},
339: 		make(chan clablabruntime.Event),
340: 	)
341: 	target := interfaceTestSample("r1", time.Now(), nil, nil).target
342: 
343: 	for range 3 {
344: 		links, err := p.nodeLinks(context.Background(), target, "e1-1,eth0,lo")
345: 		if err != nil {
346: 			t.Fatal(err)
347: 		}
348: 		if len(links) != 1 || links[0].Alias != "ethernet-1/1" {
349: 			t.Fatalf("links = %+v, want the node's own link", links)
350: 		}
351: 	}
352: 	if listing.calls != 1 {
353: 		t.Fatalf("listed %d times, want once while the interfaces stay the same", listing.calls)
354: 	}
355: 
356: 	if _, err := p.nodeLinks(context.Background(), target, "e1-1,e1-2,eth0,lo"); err != nil {
357: 		t.Fatal(err)
358: 	}
359: 	if listing.calls != 2 {
360: 		t.Fatalf("listed %d times, want again after the interfaces changed", listing.calls)
361: 	}
362: 
363: 	p.forgetListings(map[string]bool{})
364: 	if len(p.listings) != 0 {
365: 		t.Fatalf("listings of gone pods kept: %+v", p.listings)
366: 	}
367: }

369: func TestContainerTransitionActions(t *testing.T) {
370: 	t.Parallel()
371: 
372: 	const (
373: 		created = clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
374: 		running = clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
375: 		exited  = clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
376: 		healthy = clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy
377: 		start   = clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting
378: 		sick    = clablabruntime.ContainerHealthUnhealthy
379: 	)
380: 	tracked := func(state, health, pod string) *trackedContainer {
381: 		return &trackedContainer{state: state, health: health, pod: pod}
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	tests := []struct {
385: 		name     string
386: 		previous *trackedContainer
387: 		next     *trackedContainer
388: 		want     string
389: 	}{
390: 		{"new pending node", nil, tracked(created, "", ""), "create"},
391: 		{
392: 			"new running node", nil, tracked(running, start, "p1"),
393: 			"create,start,health_status: starting",
394: 		},
395: 		{
396: 			"new ready node", nil, tracked(running, healthy, "p1"),
397: 			"create,start,health_status: healthy",
398: 		},
399: 		{"new stopped node", nil, tracked(exited, "", ""), "create,stop"},
400: 		{
401: 			"pod starts", tracked(created, "", "p1"), tracked(running, start, "p1"),
402: 			"start,health_status: starting",
403: 		},
404: 		{
405: 			"device ready", tracked(running, start, "p1"), tracked(running, healthy, "p1"),
406: 			"health_status: healthy",
407: 		},
408: 		{"still booting", tracked(running, start, "p1"), tracked(running, start, "p1"), ""},
409: 		{"no change", tracked(running, healthy, "p1"), tracked(running, healthy, "p1"), ""},
410: 		{
411: 			"device not ready again", tracked(running, healthy, "p1"), tracked(running, sick, "p1"),
412: 			"health_status: unhealthy",
413: 		},
414: 		{"stop", tracked(running, healthy, "p1"), tracked(exited, "", ""), "kill,stop,die"},
415: 		{
416: 			"start", tracked(exited, "", ""), tracked(running, healthy, "p2"),
417: 			"start,health_status: healthy",
418: 		},
419: 		{
420: 			"restart, new pod pending", tracked(running, healthy, "p1"), tracked(created, "", "p2"),
421: 			"kill,stop,die",
422: 		},
423: 		{
424: 			"restart, new pod running", tracked(running, healthy, "p1"),
425: 			tracked(running, start, "p2"), "kill,stop,die,start,health_status: starting",
426: 		},
427: 		{"stopped before it ran", tracked(created, "", "p1"), tracked(exited, "", ""), "stop"},
428: 		{"stopped node rescheduled", tracked(exited, "", ""), tracked(created, "", "p2"), ""},
429: 	}
430: 	for _, tt := range tests {
431: 		got := strings.Join(containerTransitionActions(tt.previous, tt.next), ",")
432: 		if got != tt.want {
433: 			t.Fatalf("%s: actions = %q, want %q", tt.name, got, tt.want)
434: 		}
435: 	}
436: 
437: 	if got := strings.Join(containerRemovalActions(tracked(running, healthy, "p1")), ","); got !=
438: 		"kill,die,destroy" {
439: 		t.Fatalf("removal of a running node = %q", got)
440: 	}
441: 	if got := strings.Join(
442: 		containerRemovalActions(tracked(exited, "", "")),
443: 		",",
444: 	); got != "destroy" {
445: 		t.Fatalf("removal of a stopped node = %q", got)
446: 	}
447: 
448: 	// health: a running node that was healthy and is not ready anymore in the same pod is
449: 	// unhealthy; in a new pod it starts again
450: 	previous := tracked(running, healthy, "p1")
451: 	if got := containerHealth(previous, tracked(running, "", "p1"), start); got != sick {
452: 		t.Fatalf("health in the same pod = %q", got)
453: 	}
454: 	if got := containerHealth(previous, tracked(running, "", "p2"), start); got != start {
455: 		t.Fatalf("health in a new pod = %q", got)
456: 	}
457: }

459: // trackerTestNode is a Node of lab1 in lab-ns.
460: func trackerTestNode(
461: 	name string,
462: 	runState string,
463: 	conditions ...map[string]any,
464: ) *unstructured.Unstructured {
465: 	status := map[string]any{
466: 		"readiness":        "notready",
467: 		"directContainers": []any{map[string]any{"name": "node-" + name, "id": name}},
468: 	}
469: 	rawConditions := []any{}
470: 	for _, condition := range conditions {
471: 		rawConditions = append(rawConditions, condition)
472: 		if condition["type"] == "Ready" && condition["status"] == "True" {
473: 			status["readiness"] = "ready"
474: 		}
475: 	}
476: 	status["conditions"] = rawConditions
477: 
478: 	return &unstructured.Unstructured{Object: map[string]any{
479: 		"apiVersion": c9sAPIVersion,
480: 		"kind":       "Node",
481: 		"metadata": map[string]any{
482: 			"name": name, "namespace": "lab-ns", "uid": "uid-" + name,
483: 			"labels": map[string]any{
484: 				labelTopologyOwner: "lab1", labelOriginalNodeName: strings.ToUpper(name),
485: 			},
486: 		},
487: 		"spec":   map[string]any{"kind": "linux", "image": "alpine", "runState": runState},
488: 		"status": status,
489: 	}}
490: }
491: 
492: func condition(conditionType, status string) map[string]any {
493: 	return map[string]any{"type": conditionType, "status": status}
494: }

510: func newTrackerHarness(
511: 	t *testing.T,
512: 	node *unstructured.Unstructured,
513: 	pods ...*corev1.Pod,

515: 	t.Helper()

519: 		kubeObjects = append(kubeObjects, pod)

523: 	sink := make(chan clablabruntime.Event, 64)

525: 	return &trackerHarness{
526: 		t: t, r: r, sink: sink,
527: 		tracker: &containerTracker{r: r, sink: sink, nodes: map[string]*trackedContainer{}},
528: 	}

569: // refresh reads lab1 again and returns the reported actions with their state attribute.
570: func (h *trackerHarness) refresh() string {
571: 	h.t.Helper()
572: 
573: 	if !h.tracker.refresh(context.Background(), labRef{namespace: "lab-ns", lab: "lab1"}) {
574: 		h.t.Fatal("refresh failed")
575: 	}
576: 
577: 	var actions []string
578: 	for _, ev := range drain(h.sink) {
579: 		if ev.Type != clablabruntime.EventTypeContainer || ev.ActorID != "lab-ns/lab1/r1" ||
580: 			ev.ActorFullID != "lab-ns/lab1/r1" || ev.ActorName != "lab1-r1" ||
581: 			ev.Lab == nil || ev.Node == nil || ev.Node.TopologyName != "R1" ||
582: 			ev.Attributes["lab"] != "lab1" || ev.Attributes["node"] != "r1" ||
583: 			ev.Attributes["namespace"] != "lab-ns" {
584: 			h.t.Fatalf("container event = %+v", ev)
585: 		}
586: 		action := ev.Action + "=" + ev.Attributes["state"]
587: 		if signal := ev.Attributes["signal"]; signal != "" {
588: 			action += "/" + signal
589: 		}
590: 		actions = append(actions, action)
591: 	}
592: 
593: 	return strings.Join(actions, ",")
594: }

596: // TestContainerTrackerReportsTheNodeLifecycle drives one node through boot, readiness, stop,
597: // start, restart and removal on the fake cluster and checks the Docker container events.
598: func TestContainerTrackerReportsTheNodeLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
599: 	t.Parallel()
600: 
601: 	node := trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning)
602: 	h := newTrackerHarness(t, node, trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-a", corev1.PodPending))
603: 	h.seed(true)
604: 	snapshot := drain(h.sink)
605: 	if len(snapshot) != 1 || snapshot[0].Action != "created" ||
606: 		snapshot[0].Attributes["origin"] != clablabruntime.EventOriginSnapshot ||
607: 		snapshot[0].Attributes["state"] != "created" {
608: 		t.Fatalf("snapshot = %+v", snapshot)
609: 	}
610: 
611: 	// the pod runs, the device boots
612: 	h.deletePod("lab1-r1-a")
613: 	h.addPod(trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-a", corev1.PodRunning))
614: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "start=running,health_status: starting=running" {
615: 		t.Fatalf("pod running: %s", got)
616: 	}
617: 
618: 	// the device is ready
619: 	h.setNode(trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning,
620: 		condition("Ready", "True"), condition(nodeConditionContainersReady, "True")))
621: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "health_status: healthy=running" {
622: 		t.Fatalf("ready: %s", got)
623: 	}
624: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "" {
625: 		t.Fatalf("unchanged: %s", got)
626: 	}
627: 
628: 	// stop: the Node is stopped and its pod goes
629: 	h.setNode(trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateStopped,
630: 		condition(nodeConditionStopped, "True")))
631: 	h.deletePod("lab1-r1-a")
632: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "kill=running/15,stop=exited,die=exited" {
633: 		t.Fatalf("stop: %s", got)
634: 	}
635: 
636: 	// start: a new pod
637: 	h.setNode(trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning))
638: 	h.addPod(trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-b", corev1.PodPending))
639: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "" {
640: 		t.Fatalf("start requested: %s", got)
641: 	}
642: 	h.deletePod("lab1-r1-b")
643: 	h.addPod(trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-b", corev1.PodRunning))
644: 	h.setNode(
645: 		trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning, condition(nodeConditionContainersReady, "True")),
646: 	)
647: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "start=running,health_status: healthy=running" {
648: 		t.Fatalf("started: %s", got)
649: 	}
650: 
651: 	// restart: the pod is replaced
652: 	h.deletePod("lab1-r1-b")
653: 	h.addPod(trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-c", corev1.PodRunning))
654: 	if got := h.refresh(); got !=
655: 		"kill=running/15,stop=exited,die=exited,start=running,health_status: healthy=running" {
656: 		t.Fatalf("restart: %s", got)
657: 	}
658: 
659: 	// destroy
660: 	if err := h.r.client.Resource(nodeGVR).Namespace("lab-ns").
661: 		Delete(context.Background(), "r1", metav1.DeleteOptions{}); err != nil {
662: 		t.Fatal(err)
663: 	}
664: 	if got := h.refresh(); got != "kill=running/15,die=exited,destroy=exited" {
665: 		t.Fatalf("destroy: %s", got)
666: 	}
667: 	if len(h.tracker.nodes) != 0 {
668: 		t.Fatalf("destroyed node still tracked: %+v", h.tracker.nodes)
669: 	}
670: }

686: func TestNodeContainerState(t *testing.T) {
687: 	t.Parallel()
688: 
689: 	deleting := metav1.NewTime(time.Now())
690: 	pod := func(phase corev1.PodPhase, deleted bool) *corev1.Pod {
691: 		p := &corev1.Pod{Status: corev1.PodStatus{Phase: phase}}
692: 		if deleted {
693: 			p.DeletionTimestamp = &deleting
694: 		}
695: 
696: 		return p
697: 	}
698: 
699: 	tests := []struct {
700: 		name          string
701: 		stopRequested bool
702: 		pod           *corev1.Pod
703: 		want          string
704: 	}{
705: 		{"no pod yet", false, nil, "created"},
706: 		{"pod scheduled, init containers", false, pod(corev1.PodPending, false), "created"},
707: 		{"device containers run", false, pod(corev1.PodRunning, false), "running"},
708: 		{"pod being deleted (restart)", false, pod(corev1.PodRunning, true), "exited"},
709: 		{"pod ended", false, pod(corev1.PodFailed, false), "exited"},
710: 		{"stop requested, pod terminating", true, pod(corev1.PodRunning, true), "exited"},
711: 		{"stopped", true, nil, "exited"},
712: 	}
713: 	for _, tt := range tests {
714: 		if got := nodeContainerState(tt.stopRequested, tt.pod); got != tt.want {
715: 			t.Fatalf("%s: %q, want %q", tt.name, got, tt.want)
716: 		}
717: 	}
718: }

720: func TestNewestPodPrefersAPodThatIsNotDeleted(t *testing.T) {
721: 	t.Parallel()
722: 
723: 	now := time.Now()
724: 	deleting := metav1.NewTime(now)
725: 	old := &corev1.Pod{
726: 		ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{
727: 			Name: "old", CreationTimestamp: metav1.NewTime(now.Add(-time.Hour)),
728: 			DeletionTimestamp: &deleting,
729: 		},
730: 		Status: corev1.PodStatus{Phase: corev1.PodRunning},
731: 	}
732: 	replacement := &corev1.Pod{
733: 		ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "new", CreationTimestamp: metav1.NewTime(now)},
734: 		Status:     corev1.PodStatus{Phase: corev1.PodPending},
735: 	}
736: 	if got := newestPod(old, replacement); got != replacement {
737: 		t.Fatalf("newestPod = %s, want the replacement", got.Name)
738: 	}
739: 	if got := newestPod(replacement, old); got != replacement {
740: 		t.Fatalf("newestPod = %s, want the replacement", got.Name)
741: 	}
742: }

744: func TestEnrichStateReportsContainerStateAndHealth(t *testing.T) {
745: 	t.Parallel()
746: 
747: 	r := newTestRuntimeWithKubeObjects(
748: 		[]*unstructured.Unstructured{
749: 			trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning, condition("Ready", "True")),
750: 			// its peer is stopped: not ready, but the device is
751: 			trackerTestNode("r2", nodeRunStateRunning,
752: 				condition(nodeConditionContainersReady, "True")),
753: 			trackerTestNode("r3", nodeRunStateRunning),
754: 			trackerTestNode("r4", nodeRunStateStopped, condition(nodeConditionStopped, "True")),
755: 		},
756: 		[]k8sruntime.Object{
757: 			captureTestPod("lab1-r1-a", "r1"),
758: 			captureTestPod("lab1-r2-a", "r2"),
759: 			withNodeUID(captureTestPod("lab1-r3-a", "r3"), "uid-r3"),
760: 			// the newer pod of an earlier Node r3 that still terminates is not r3's pod
761: 			withNodeUID(withCreation(captureTestPod("lab1-r3-stale", "r3"), time.Hour), "uid-old"),
762: 		},
763: 	)
764: 
765: 	state := &clablabruntime.LabState{Name: "lab1", Namespace: "lab-ns"}
766: 	if err := r.enrichState(context.Background(), state); err != nil {
767: 		t.Fatal(err)
768: 	}
769: 
770: 	want := map[string]string{
771: 		"r1": "running/healthy", "r2": "running/healthy", "r3": "running/starting", "r4": "exited/",
772: 	}
773: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
774: 		if node.Name == "r3" && node.Pod != "lab1-r3-a" {
775: 			t.Fatalf("r3 pod = %q, want its own Node's pod", node.Pod)
776: 		}
777: 		if got := node.ContainerState + "/" + node.Health; got != want[node.Name] {
778: 			t.Fatalf("%s = %s, want %s", node.Name, got, want[node.Name])
779: 		}
780: 		if node.TopologyName != strings.ToUpper(node.Name) {
781: 			t.Fatalf("%s topology name = %q", node.Name, node.TopologyName)
782: 		}
783: 	}
784: }

799: func sourceDeployRequest(path string, noTopologyCR bool) clablabruntime.DeployRequest {
800: 	return clablabruntime.DeployRequest{
801: 		Name:               "lab1",

809: // TestDeployRecordsTheTopologyFile checks where a deploy records the topology file and that

811: func TestDeployRecordsTheTopologyFile(t *testing.T) {
812: 	t.Parallel()
813: 
814: 	// with a Topology resource: on the Topology, updated by every deploy
815: 	r := newTestRuntime()
816: 	if _, err := r.Deploy(context.Background(),
817: 		sourceDeployRequest("/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml", false)); err != nil {
818: 		t.Fatal(err)
