2556: +// trackerTestNode is a Node of lab1 in lab-ns.
2557: +func trackerTestNode(
2558: +	name string,
2559: +	runState string,
2560: +	conditions ...map[string]any,
2561: +) *unstructured.Unstructured {
2562: +	status := map[string]any{
2563: +		"readiness":        "notready",
2564: +		"directContainers": []any{map[string]any{"name": "node-" + name, "id": name}},
2565: +	}
2566: +	rawConditions := []any{}
2567: +	for _, condition := range conditions {
2568: +		rawConditions = append(rawConditions, condition)
2569: +		if condition["type"] == "Ready" && condition["status"] == "True" {
2570: +			status["readiness"] = "ready"
2571: +		}
2572: +	}
2573: +	status["conditions"] = rawConditions
2574: +
2575: +	return &unstructured.Unstructured{Object: map[string]any{
2576: +		"apiVersion": c9sAPIVersion,
2577: +		"kind":       "Node",
2578: +		"metadata": map[string]any{
2579: +			"name": name, "namespace": "lab-ns", "uid": "uid-" + name,
2580: +			"labels": map[string]any{
2581: +				labelTopologyOwner: "lab1", labelOriginalNodeName: strings.ToUpper(name),
2582: +			},
2583: +		},
2584: +		"spec":   map[string]any{"kind": "linux", "image": "alpine", "runState": runState},
2585: +		"status": status,
2586: +	}}
2587: +}
2588: +
2589: +func condition(conditionType, status string) map[string]any {
2590: +	return map[string]any{"type": conditionType, "status": status}
2591: +}
2592: +
2593: +func trackerTestPod(name string, phase corev1.PodPhase) *corev1.Pod {
2594: +	pod := captureTestPod(name, "r1")
2595: +	pod.Status.Phase = phase
2596: +
2597: +	return pod
2598: +}

2600: +type trackerHarness struct {
2601: +	t       *testing.T
2602: +	r       *Runtime
2603: +	tracker *containerTracker
2604: +	sink    chan clablabruntime.Event
2605: +}
2606: +
2607: +func newTrackerHarness(
2608: +	t *testing.T,
2609: +	node *unstructured.Unstructured,
2610: +	pods ...*corev1.Pod,
2611: +) *trackerHarness {
2612: +	t.Helper()
2613: +
2614: +	kubeObjects := make([]k8sruntime.Object, 0, len(pods))
2615: +	for _, pod := range pods {
2616: +		kubeObjects = append(kubeObjects, pod)
2617: +	}
2618: +	r := newTestRuntimeWithKubeObjects([]*unstructured.Unstructured{node}, kubeObjects)
2619: +	r.labNamespaceOverride = "lab-ns"
2620: +	sink := make(chan clablabruntime.Event, 64)
2621: +
2622: +	return &trackerHarness{
2623: +		t: t, r: r, sink: sink,
2624: +		tracker: &containerTracker{r: r, sink: sink, nodes: map[string]*trackedContainer{}},
2625: +	}
2626: +}

2628: +func (h *trackerHarness) seed(snapshot bool) {
2629: +	h.t.Helper()
2630: +
2631: +	state, err := h.r.Inspect(context.Background(), clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1"})
2632: +	if err != nil {
2633: +		h.t.Fatal(err)
2634: +	}
2635: +	h.tracker.observeLab(context.Background(), labRef{namespace: "lab-ns", lab: "lab1"}, state,
2636: +		&observeSeed{snapshot: snapshot})
2637: +}

2643: +		Update(context.Background(), node, metav1.UpdateOptions{}); err != nil {

2666: +// refresh reads lab1 again and returns the reported actions with their state attribute.
2667: +func (h *trackerHarness) refresh() string {
2668: +	h.t.Helper()
2669: +
2670: +	if !h.tracker.refresh(context.Background(), labRef{namespace: "lab-ns", lab: "lab1"}) {
2671: +		h.t.Fatal("refresh failed")
2672: +	}
2673: +
2674: +	var actions []string
2675: +	for _, ev := range drain(h.sink) {
2676: +		if ev.Type != clablabruntime.EventTypeContainer || ev.ActorID != "lab-ns/lab1/r1" ||
2677: +			ev.ActorFullID != "lab-ns/lab1/r1" || ev.ActorName != "lab1-r1" ||
2678: +			ev.Lab == nil || ev.Node == nil || ev.Node.TopologyName != "R1" ||
2679: +			ev.Attributes["lab"] != "lab1" || ev.Attributes["node"] != "r1" ||
2680: +			ev.Attributes["namespace"] != "lab-ns" {
2681: +			h.t.Fatalf("container event = %+v", ev)
2682: +		}
2683: +		action := ev.Action + "=" + ev.Attributes["state"]
2684: +		if signal := ev.Attributes["signal"]; signal != "" {
2685: +			action += "/" + signal
2686: +		}
2687: +		actions = append(actions, action)
2688: +	}
2689: +
2690: +	return strings.Join(actions, ",")
2691: +}
2692: +
2693: +// TestContainerTrackerReportsTheNodeLifecycle drives one node through boot, readiness, stop,
2694: +// start, restart and removal on the fake cluster and checks the Docker container events.
2695: +func TestContainerTrackerReportsTheNodeLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
2696: +	t.Parallel()
2697: +
2698: +	node := trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning)
2699: +	h := newTrackerHarness(t, node, trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-a", corev1.PodPending))
2700: +	h.seed(true)
2701: +	snapshot := drain(h.sink)
2702: +	if len(snapshot) != 1 || snapshot[0].Action != "created" ||
2703: +		snapshot[0].Attributes["origin"] != clablabruntime.EventOriginSnapshot ||
2704: +		snapshot[0].Attributes["state"] != "created" {
2705: +		t.Fatalf("snapshot = %+v", snapshot)
2706: +	}
2707: +
2708: +	// the pod runs, the device boots
2709: +	h.deletePod("lab1-r1-a")
2710: +	h.addPod(trackerTestPod("lab1-r1-a", corev1.PodRunning))
2711: +	if got := h.refresh(); got != "start=running,health_status: starting=running" {
2712: +		t.Fatalf("pod running: %s", got)
2713: +	}
2714: +
2715: +	// the device is ready
2716: +	h.setNode(trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateRunning,
2717: +		condition("Ready", "True"), condition(nodeConditionContainersReady, "True")))
2718: +	if got := h.refresh(); got != "health_status: healthy=running" {
2719: +		t.Fatalf("ready: %s", got)
2720: +	}
2721: +	if got := h.refresh(); got != "" {
2722: +		t.Fatalf("unchanged: %s", got)
2723: +	}
2724: +
2725: +	// stop: the Node is stopped and its pod goes
2726: +	h.setNode(trackerTestNode("r1", nodeRunStateStopped,
2727: +		condition(nodeConditionStopped, "True")))
2728: +	h.deletePod("lab1-r1-a")

2817: +func TestNewestPodPrefersAPodThatIsNotDeleted(t *testing.T) {
2818: +	t.Parallel()
2819: +
2820: +	now := time.Now()
2821: +	deleting := metav1.NewTime(now)
2822: +	old := &corev1.Pod{
2823: +		ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{
2824: +			Name: "old", CreationTimestamp: metav1.NewTime(now.Add(-time.Hour)),
2825: +			DeletionTimestamp: &deleting,
2826: +		},
2827: +		Status: corev1.PodStatus{Phase: corev1.PodRunning},
2828: +	}
2829: +	replacement := &corev1.Pod{
2830: +		ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "new", CreationTimestamp: metav1.NewTime(now)},
2831: +		Status:     corev1.PodStatus{Phase: corev1.PodPending},
2832: +	}
2833: +	if got := newestPod(old, replacement); got != replacement {
2834: +		t.Fatalf("newestPod = %s, want the replacement", got.Name)
2835: +	}
2836: +	if got := newestPod(replacement, old); got != replacement {
2837: +		t.Fatalf("newestPod = %s, want the replacement", got.Name)
2838: +	}
2839: +}

2908: +func TestDeployRecordsTheTopologyFile(t *testing.T) {
2909: +	t.Parallel()
2910: +
2911: +	// with a Topology resource: on the Topology, updated by every deploy
2912: +	r := newTestRuntime()
2913: +	if _, err := r.Deploy(context.Background(),
2914: +		sourceDeployRequest("/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml", false)); err != nil {
2915: +		t.Fatal(err)
2916: +	}
2917: +	topology := getTestTopology(t, r, "lab-ns", "lab1")
2918: +	if got := topology.GetAnnotations()[annotationTopologyFile]; got != "/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml" {
2919: +		t.Fatalf("Topology annotation = %q", got)
2920: +	}
2921: +	state, err := r.Inspect(context.Background(),
2922: +		clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1", Namespace: "lab-ns"})
2923: +	if err != nil {
2924: +		t.Fatal(err)
2925: +	}
2926: +	if state.TopologyPath != "/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml" {
2927: +		t.Fatalf("TopologyPath = %q", state.TopologyPath)
2928: +	}
2929: +
2930: +	if _, err := r.Deploy(context.Background(),
2931: +		sourceDeployRequest("/srv/labs/lab1.clab.yml", false)); err != nil {
2932: +		t.Fatal(err)
2933: +	}
2934: +	topology = getTestTopology(t, r, "lab-ns", "lab1")
2935: +	if got := topology.GetAnnotations()[annotationTopologyFile]; got != "/srv/labs/lab1.clab.yml" {
2936: +		t.Fatalf("Topology annotation after a deploy from another file = %q", got)
2937: +	}
2938: +
2939: +	// without a Topology resource: on the Nodes only, kept from their creation
2940: +	r = newTestRuntime()
2941: +	if _, err := r.Deploy(context.Background(),
2942: +		sourceDeployRequest("/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml", true)); err != nil {
2943: +		t.Fatal(err)
2944: +	}
2945: +	assertPrimitiveTopologyFile(t, r, "/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml")
2946: +	state, err = r.Inspect(context.Background(),
2947: +		clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1", Namespace: "lab-ns"})
2948: +	if err != nil {
2949: +		t.Fatal(err)
2950: +	}
2951: +	if state.TopologyPath != "/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml" {
2952: +		t.Fatalf("TopologyPath without a Topology = %q", state.TopologyPath)
2953: +	}
2954: +
2955: +	plan, err := r.Plan(context.Background(),
2956: +		sourceDeployRequest("/srv/labs/lab1.clab.yml", true))
2957: +	if err != nil {
2958: +		t.Fatal(err)
2959: +	}
2960: +	for _, change := range plan.Changes {
2961: +		if change.Kind == "Node" {
2962: +			t.Fatalf("a deploy from another file would change %+v and replace its pod", change)
2963: +		}
2964: +	}
2965: +	if _, err := r.Deploy(context.Background(),
2966: +		sourceDeployRequest("/srv/labs/lab1.clab.yml", true)); err != nil {
2967: +		t.Fatal(err)
2968: +	}
2969: +	assertPrimitiveTopologyFile(t, r, "/home/alice/labs/lab1.clab.yml")
2970: +}

2997: +	}

3012: +		}}

3015: +
3016: +	updated := reconciledPrimitiveObject(

3018: +		desired,

3020: +	if got := updated.GetAnnotations()[annotationTopologyFile]; got != "/old.clab.yml" {
3021: +		t.Fatalf("existing Node file = %q, want it kept", got)
3022: +	}
3023: +
3024: +	// a Node deployed before containerlab recorded files does not get one
3025: +	existing := node(nil)

3029: +		t.Fatalf("Node without a file = %+v", updated.GetAnnotations())

3031: +
3032: +	// the Topology always records the latest file
3033: +	topology := topologyObject("lab1", "lab-ns", "", "topology:\n")
3034: +	setTopologySourceFile(topology, "/old.clab.yml")
3035: +	newTopology := topologyObject("lab1", "lab-ns", "", "topology:\n")
3036: +	setTopologySourceFile(newTopology, "/new.clab.yml")
3037: +	updated = reconciledPrimitiveObject(topology, newTopology)
3038: +	if got := updated.GetAnnotations()[annotationTopologyFile]; got != "/new.clab.yml" {
3039: +		t.Fatalf("Topology file = %q", got)

4193: +// such effect and always records the file of the latest deploy.
4194: +func carryOverNodeTopologyFile(existing, updated *unstructured.Unstructured) {

4526: +// nodeHealth is the health of a running node: healthy once the Node is ready or its device

4528: +// healthcheck: a node whose links wait for a stopped peer is not ready, but its device is.

4536: +			return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy
4537: +		}
4538: +	}
4539: +
4540: +	return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting
4541: +}

The runtime renames the nodes Kubernetes cannot carry, so the state it reports does not\n// always use the name the topology file wrote.\nfunc (c *CLab) topologyNodeName(name string) string {\n\tif c.Config.Topology == nil {\n\t\treturn name\n\t}\n\tif _, ok := c.Config.Topology.Nodes[name]; ok {\n\t\treturn name\n\t}\n\n\tfor nodeName := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {\n\t\tif clabnames.SanitizeName(nodeName) == name {\n\t\t\treturn nodeName\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn name\n}\n\n// managementAddress reports the address a user reaches the node at: the LoadBalancer address\n// when the node is exposed, otherwise the allocated management address.\nfunc managementAddress(node clablabruntime.NodeState) clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs {\n\tsettings := clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs{}\n\n\tif ip := net.ParseIP(node.LoadBalancerAddress); ip != nil {\n\t\tif ip.To4() != nil {\n\t\t\tsettings.IPv4addr = node.LoadBalancerAddress\n\t\t\tsettings.IPv4pLen = 32\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tsettings.IPv6addr = node.LoadBalancerAddress\n\t\t\tsettings.IPv6pLen = 128\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif settings.IPv4addr == \"\" {\n\t\tsettings.IPv4addr, settings.IPv4pLen = splitManagementCIDR(node.MgmtIPv4Address)\n\t}\n\tif settings.IPv6addr == \"\" {\n\t\tsettings.IPv6addr, settings.IPv6pLen = splitManagementCIDR(node.MgmtIPv6Address)\n\t}\n",

// LinkOperState represents the operational state of the interface.
type LinkOperState uint16

const (
	OperUnknown LinkOperState = 0
	OperNotPresent LinkOperState = 1
	OperDown LinkOperState = 2
	OperLowerLayerDown LinkOperState = 3
	OperTesting LinkOperState = 4
	OperDormant LinkOperState = 5
	OperUp LinkOperState = 6
)

func (s LinkOperState) String() string {
	switch s {
	case OperNotPresent:
		return "notPresent"
	case OperDown:
		return "down"
	case OperLowerLayerDown:
		return "lowerlayerdown"
	case OperTesting:
		return "testing"
	case OperDormant:
		return "dormant"
	case OperUp:
		return "up"
	}
	return "unknown"
}

1083:  With `--runtime c9s`, events are backed by kubernetes watches for Clabernetes
1084: -`Topology` and `Node` resources and labeled Pods. Interface state (`interface up`
1085: -and `interface down` events) and statistics are sampled inside the device

1090: +`Topology` and `Node` resources and labeled Pods. They use the actions and
1091: +attributes of the Docker runtime: a node is a container (`create`, `start`,
1092: +`kill`, `stop`, `die`, `destroy`, `health_status: …`) described by the same
1093: +labels, and the interface events (`snapshot`, `create`, `update`, `delete`,
1094: +`stats`) report the node's lab link interfaces, `eth0` and `lo` under the names
1095: +a Docker container of the node has. Interface state and statistics are sampled
1096: +inside the device containers, not through local host netlink. The stream covers
1097: +every namespace by default; `--namespace` (or `CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE`) limits it
1098: +to one namespace, and `-t`/`--name` to one lab. With Docker and Podman the lab
1099: +selection is ignored and every lab is streamed. The
1100: +[c9s runtime manual](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#events) lists the
1101: +attributes and the few Docker attributes c9s has no equivalent for.

1115: @@ -3,11 +3,11 @@
1116:  ### Description
1117:  
1118:  The `inspect interfaces` subcommand provides information about the network interfaces of deployed nodes of a deployed lab.
1119:  The subcommand gathers information directly from deployed containers, and displays information about their operational state, network interface type, and if applicable, the applied network interface alias.
1120:  
1121: -With the [c9s runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture), the listing covers the lab link interfaces of each running node, the ones [`capture`](../capture.md) accepts, with the alias the topology used, and the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read in the node's device container. The node names follow `inspect` (`<lab>-<node>`), and the JSON fields are the same as with Docker.
1122: +With the [c9s runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#interface-events), the listing covers the interfaces a Docker container of the node has: the lab link interfaces of each running node (the ones [`capture`](../capture.md) accepts) with the alias the topology used, the management interface `eth0` and the loopback `lo`, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read in the node's device container. The pod's own interfaces are not listed. The node names follow `inspect` (`<lab>-<node>`), and the JSON fields and values (`veth`/`device`, netlink state names) are the same as with Docker. `eth0` and `lo` cannot be captured on c9s.
1123:  
1124:  ### Usage
1125:  
1126:  `containerlab [global-flags] inspect interfaces [local-flags]`

1149: +
1150: +A deploy records the absolute path of the topology file, on the machine that
1151: +deployed it, in the annotation `containerlab.dev/topo-file`:
1152: +
1153: +- with a `Topology` resource, on the `Topology`; every deploy records the file
1154: +  it read
1155: +- with `--no-topology-cr`, on every `Node`. clabernetes copies a Node's
1156: +  annotations into its pod, so a Node keeps the file it was created from: a
1157: +  later deploy from another file does not change it and does not restart the
1158: +  node. Destroy and deploy again to record a new file.
1159: +
1160: +`inspect` reports the recorded file as `labPath` and `absLabPath` (shortened
1161: +for the table, as for Docker), and events as `clab-topo-file`, so a client
1162: +matches a running lab to its file the same way for every runtime. The file is a
1163: +path on the deploying machine; a client on another machine cannot assume it
1164: +exists there.
1165: +
1166: +A lab that containerlab did not deploy from a file, for example one applied from
1167: +`deploy --emit-crs` output with `kubectl` (the emitted manifests do not carry
1168: +the annotation), has no recorded file. It reports where its definition lives in
1169: +the cluster: `k8s://<namespace>/topologies/<lab>`, or
1170: +`k8s://<namespace>/labs/<lab>` without a `Topology` resource. With `-t`,
1171: +`inspect` reports the given file.
1172: +
1173:  Useful kubernetes checks for the same state are:
1174:  
1175:  ```bash
1176:  kubectl -n <namespace> get node.c9s.run,link.c9s.run,nodeprofile.c9s.run,deploy,pod,svc,cm,pvc \
1177:    -l c9s.run/topologyOwner=<lab>

346: +func attributeKeys(attributes map[string]string) []string {

356: +// assertAttributeParity checks that the c9s event carries every attribute of the Docker event,
357: +// apart from the ones listed.
358: +func assertAttributeParity(t *testing.T, docker, c9s aggregatedEvent, dockerOnly map[string]bool) {
359: +	t.Helper()
360: +
361: +	dockerAttributes := mergedEventAttributes(docker)
362: +	c9sAttributes := mergedEventAttributes(c9s)
363: +	var missing []string
364: +	for key := range dockerAttributes {
365: +		if _, ok := c9sAttributes[key]; !ok && !dockerOnly[key] {
366: +			missing = append(missing, key)
367: +		}
368: +	}
369: +	if len(missing) != 0 {
370: +		sort.Strings(missing)
371: +		t.Fatalf("c9s %s %s lacks %v\ndocker: %v\nc9s:    %v", c9s.Type, c9s.Action, missing,
372: +			attributeKeys(dockerAttributes), attributeKeys(c9sAttributes))
373: +	}
374: +}

546: +// dockerInterfaceEvent is a netlink interface event of a Docker container.

561: +	}

\"github.com/docker/docker/api/types/events\"\n+\tclabconstants \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants\"\n+\tclabcore \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/core\"\n+\tclablabruntime \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime\"\n+\tclabruntime \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime\"\n+\tclabtypes \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types\"\n+\tclabutils \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils\"\n+)\n+\n+// These tests build the events the Docker runtime and the c9s lab runtime report for the same\n+// node and compare them: every attribute a Docker event carries is in the c9s event, with the\n+// same meaning, apart from the ones c9s has no equivalent for.\n+\n+// dockerOnlyContainerAttributes are the Docker container event attributes c9s has no\n+// equivalent for: the Docker event scope, the Docker management bridge, and the exit code and\n+// run time of a container process, which Kubernetes does not keep once the pod is gone.\n+var dockerOnlyContainerAttributes = map[string]bool{ //nolint:gochecknoglobals\n+\t\"scope\":                     true,\n+\tclabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr: true,\n+\tclabconstants.NodeLabDir:    true,\n+\t\"exitCode\":                  true,\n+\t\"execDuration\":              true,\n+}\n+\n+const parityTopology = `name: parity\n+mgmt:\n+  network: clab\n+topology:\n+  nodes:\n+    client:\n+      kind: linux\n+      image: ghcr.io/srl-labs/network-multitool\n+    srl1:\n+      kind: nokia_srlinux\n+      image: ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux:25.10\n+  links:\n+    - endpoints: [\"client:eth1\", \"srl1:ethernet-1/1\"]\n+`\n+\n+// parityLab loads the topology as a Docker deploy does and returns its labels per node.\n+func parityLab(t *testing.T) (string, *clabcore.CLab) {\n+\tt.Helper()\n+\n+\tdir := t.TempDir()\n+\tpath := filepath.Join(dir, \"parity.clab.yml\")\n+\tif err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(parityTopology), 0o600); err != nil {\n+\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n+\t}\n+\tt.Setenv(\"USER\", \"alice\")\n+\tt.Setenv(\"SUDO_USER\", \"\")\n+\n+\tc, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(clabcore.WithTopoPath(path, nil))\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn path, c\n+}\n+\n+// fakeDockerRuntime answers the container lookup the events command makes for a Docker event.\n+type fakeDockerRuntime struct {\n+\tclabruntime.ContainerRuntime\n+\tcontainer clabruntime.GenericContainer\n+}\n+\n+func (f *fakeDockerRuntime) ListContainers(\n+\tcontext.Context,\n+\t[]*clabtypes.GenericFilter,\n+) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {\n+\treturn []clabruntime.GenericContainer{f.container}, nil\n+}\n+\n+// dockerContainer is the container Docker runs for a node.\n+func dockerContainer(t *testing.T, c *clabcore.CLab, node string) clabruntime.GenericContainer {\n+\tt.Helper()\n+\n+\tcfg := c.Nodes[node].Config()\n+\tlabels := cloneStringMap(cfg.Labels)\n+\tlabels[clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr] = \"br-92bb9fb46cd2\"\n+\n+\treturn clabruntime.GenericContainer{\n+\t\tNames:   []string{cfg.LongName},\n+\t\tID:      \"57b7763f3b4d97ff0c96b1dab8294b836199628a2d9400549948a963732e185a\",\n+\t\tShortID: \"57b7763f3b4d\",\n+\t\tImage:   cfg.Image,\n+\t\tState:   \"running\",\n+\t\tStatus:  \"Up 19 seconds\",\n+\t\tLabels:  labels,\n+\t\tNetworkSettings: clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs{\n+\t\t\tIPv4addr: \"172.20.20.2\", IPv4pLen: 24, IPv6addr: \"3fff:172:20:20::2\", IPv6pLen: 64,\n+\t\t},\n+\t\tNetworkName: \"clab\",\n+\t\tPorts: []*clabtypes.GenericPortBinding{\n+\t\t\t{ContainerPort: 22, Protocol: \"tcp\"}, {ContainerPort: 80, Protocol: \"tcp\"},\n+\t\t},\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+// dockerContainerEvent is a Docker container event as `containerlab events` reports it: the\n+// Docker message (container labels, image and name as attributes, plus the action's own) through\n+// the events command's conversion and enrichment.\n+func dockerContainerEvent(\n+\tt *testing.T,\n+\tcontainer clabruntime.GenericContainer,\n+\taction string,\n+\textra map[string]string,\n+) aggregatedEvent {\n+\tt.Helper()\n+\n+\tattributes := cloneStringMap(container.Labels)\n+\tattributes[\"image\"] = container.Image\n+\tattributes[\"name\"] = container.Names[0]\n+\tfor k, v := range extra {\n+\t\tattributes[k] = v\n+\t}\n+\tdata := clabutils.DockerMessageToEventData(dockerEvents.Message{\n+\t\tType:     dockerEvents.ContainerEventType,\n+\t\tAction:   dockerEvents.Action(action),\n+\t\tActor:    dockerEvents.Actor{ID: container.ID, Attributes: attributes},\n+\t\tScope:    \"local\",\n+\t\tTimeNano: time.Now().UnixNano(),\n+\t})\n+\n+\treturn aggregatedEventFromContainerEvent(context.Background(),\n+\t\t&fakeDockerRuntime{container: container},\n+\t\tclabruntime.ContainerEvent{\n+\t\t\tTimestamp: data.Timestamp, Type: data.Type, Action: data.Action,\n+\t\t\tActorID: data.ActorID, ActorName: data.ActorName, ActorFullID: data.ActorFullID,\n+\t\t\tAttributes: data.Attributes,\n+\t\t})\n+}\n+\n+// c9sNode is the same node as the c9s runtime reports it, deployed from the same file.\n+func c9sNode(\n+\tc *clabcore.CLab,\n+\tpath, node string,\n+) (*clablabruntime.LabState, clablabruntime.NodeState) {\n+\tcfg := c.Nodes[node].Config()\n+\tstate := &clablabruntime.LabState{\n+\t\tName: \"parity\", Namespace: \"c9s-parity\", Owner: \"alice\", TopologyPath: path,\n+\t\tState: \"running\", Ready: true,\n+\t}\n+\tnodeState := clablabruntime.NodeState{\n+\t\tName: node, Kind: cfg.Kind, Image: cfg.Image, State: \"ready\", Ready: true,\n+\t\tContainerState:  clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning,\n+\t\tHealth:          clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy,\n+\t\tMgmtIPv4Address: \"172.20.20.84/24\", MgmtIPv6Address: \"3fff:172:20:20::84/64\",\n+\t\tPod: node + \"-88598986c-rbdfq\", Container: \"node-\" + node, NodeUID: \"uid-\" + node,\n+\t\tExposedPorts: []clablabruntime.ExposedPort{\n+\t\t\t{\n+\t\t\t\tPort:       22,\n+\t\t\t\tExposePort: 22,\n+\t\t\t\tProtocol:   \"tcp\",\n+\t\t\t},\n+\t\t\t{Port: 80, ExposePort: 80, Protocol: \"tcp\"},\n+\t\t},\n+\t}\n+\tstate.Nodes = []clablabruntime.NodeState{nodeState}\n+\n+\treturn state, nodeState\n+}\n+\n+// c9sContainerEvent is the event the c9s runtime emits, as `containerlab events` reports it.\n+func c9sContainerEvent(\n+\tclab *clabcore.CLab,\n+\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState,\n+\tnode clablabruntime.NodeState,\n+\taction, containerState string,\n+\textra map[string]string,\n+) aggregatedEvent {\n+\tkey := state.Namespace + \"/\" + state.Name + \"/\" + node.Name\n+\tattributes := map[string]string{\n+\t\t\"namespace\": state.Namespace, \"lab\": state.Name, \"node\": node.Name, \"pod\": node.Pod,\n+\t\t\"state\": containerState,\n+\t}\n+\tfor k, v := range extra {\n+\t\tattributes[k] = v\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn aggregatedEventFromLabRuntimeEvent(clab, clablabruntime.Event{\n+\t\tType: clablabruntime.EventTypeContainer, Action: action,\n+\t\tActorID: key, ActorName: state.Name + \"-\" + node.Name, ActorFullID: key,\n+\t\tAttributes: attributes, Lab: state, Node: &node,\n+\t})\n+}\n+\n+func attributeKeys(attributes map[string]string) []string {\n+\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(attributes))\n+\tfor key := range attributes {\n+\t\tkeys = append(keys, key)\n+\t}\n+\tsort.Strings(keys)\n+\n+\treturn keys\n+}\n+\n+// assertAttributeParity checks that the c9s event carries every attribute of the Docker event,\n+// apart from the ones listed.\n+func assertAttributeParity(t *testing.T, docker, c9s aggregatedEvent, dockerOnly map[string]bool) {\n+\tt.Helper()\n+\n+\tdockerAttributes := mergedEventAttributes(docker)\n+\tc9sAttributes := mergedEventAttributes(c9s)\n+\tvar missing []string\n+\tfor key := range dockerAttributes {\n+\t\tif _, ok := c9sAttributes[key]; !ok && !dockerOnly[key] {\n+\t\t\tmissing = append(missing, key)\n+\t\t}\n+\t}\n+\tif len(missing) != 0 {\n+\t\tsort.Strings(missing)\n+\t\tt.Fatalf(\"c9s %s %s lacks %v\\ndocker: %v\\nc9s:    %v\", c9s.Type, c9s.Action, missing,\n+\t\t\tattributeKeys(dockerAttributes), attributeKeys(c9sAttributes))\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+// TestContainerEventParity compares the container events of a node's lifecycle, with the c9s\n+// lab read with its topology file (events -t) and without it (events --name), where the\n+// attributes come from the cluster alone.\n+func TestContainerEventParity(t *testing.T) {\n+\tpath, dockerLab := parityLab(t)\n+\tbyName, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(clabcore.WithLabNameOnly(\"parity\"))\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n+\t}\n+\n+\tfor _, mode := range []struct {\n+\t\tname string\n+\t\tlab  *clabcore.CLab\n+\t}{{\"with the topology\", dockerLab}, {\"by name\", byName}} {\n+\t\tt.Run(mode.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n+\t\t\tassertContainerEventParity(t, path, dockerLab, mode.lab, mode.lab == byName)\n+\t\t})\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+func assertContainerEventParity(\n+\tt *testing.T,\n+\tpath string,\n+\tdockerLab, c9sLab *clabcore.CLab,\n+\tbyName bool,\n+) {\n+\tt.Helper()\n+\n+\tfor _, node := range []string{\"client\", \"srl1\"} {\n+\t\tcontainer := dockerContainer(t, dockerLab, node)\n+\t\tstate, nodeState := c9sNode(dockerLab, path, node)\n+\t\tdockerOnly := dockerOnlyContainerAttributes\n+\t\tif byName && node == \"srl1\" {\n+\t\t\t// The type is the SR Linux default; the cluster has only the types a topology\n+\t\t\t// sets, so a lab read by name does not know it.\n+\t\t\tdockerOnly = map[string]bool{clabconstants.NodeType: true}\n+\t\t\tfor key := range dockerOnlyContainerAttributes {\n+\t\t\t\tdockerOnly[key] = true\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t}\n+\n+\t\tfor _, tt := range []struct {\n+\t\t\taction, state string\n+\t\t\textra         map[string]string\n+\t\t}{\n+\t\t\t{\"create\", \"created\", nil},\n+\t\t\t{\"start\", \"running\", nil},\n+\t\t\t{\"kill\", \"running\", map[string]string{\"signal\": \"15\"}},\n+\t\t\t{\"stop\", \"exited\", nil},\n+\t\t\t{\"die\", \"exited\", map[string]string{\"exitCode\": \"137\", \"execDuration\": \"3\"}},\n+\t\t\t{\"health_status: healthy\", \"running\", nil},\n+\t\t\t{\"destroy\", \"exited\", nil},\n+\t\t} {\n+\t\t\tdocker := dockerContainerEvent(t, container, tt.action, tt.extra)\n+\t\t\tvar c9sExtra map[string]string\n+\t\t\tif tt.action == \"kill\" {\n+\t\t\t\tc9sExtra = tt.extra\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\tc9s := c9sContainerEvent(c9sLab, state, nodeState, tt.action, tt.state, c9sExtra)\n+\t\t\tassertAttributeParity(t, docker, c9s, dockerOnly)\n+\n+\t\t\tgot := mergedEventAttributes(c9s)\n+\t\t\twant := map[string]string{\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.Containerlab: \"parity\",\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.NodeName:     node,\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.LongName:     \"parity-\" + node,\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.NodeKind:     dockerLab.Nodes[node].Config().Kind,\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.TopoFile:     path,\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.Owner:        \"alice\",\n+\t\t\t\t\"image\":                    container.Image,\n+\t\t\t\t\"name\":                     \"parity-\" + node,\n+\t\t\t\t\"id\":                       \"c9s-parity/parity/\" + node,\n+\t\t\t\t\"mgmt_ipv4\":                \"172.20.20.84/24\",\n+\t\t\t\t\"mgmt_ipv6\":                \"3fff:172:20:20::84/64\",\n+\t\t\t\t\"ports\":                    \"22/tcp;80/tcp\",\n+\t\t\t\t\"state\":                    tt.state,\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\tfor key, value := range want {\n+\t\t\t\tif got[key] != value {\n+\t\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s %s: %s = %q, want %q\", node, tt.action, key, got[key], value)\n+\t\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t// the label values have Docker's format\n+\t\t\tdockerAttributes := mergedEventAttributes(docker)\n+\t\t\tfor _, key := range []string{\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.Containerlab, clabconstants.NodeName, clabconstants.NodeKind,\n+\t\t\t\tclabconstants.NodeType, clabconstants.TopoFile, clabconstants.Owner, \"image\",\n+\t\t\t\t\"ports\",\n+\t\t\t} {\n+\t\t\t\tif dockerOnly[key] {\n+\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n+\t\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t\tif got[key] != dockerAttributes[key] {\n+\t\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s %s: %s = %q, docker %q\", node, tt.action, key, got[key],\n+\t\t\t\t\t\tdockerAttributes[key])\n+\t\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\tif c9s.ActorID != c9s.ActorFullID || c9s.ActorName != \"parity-\"+node {\n+\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s %s: actor = %+v\", node, tt.action, c9s)\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t}\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+// TestContainerSnapshotParity compares the --initial-state events of a running node, with the\n+// c9s lab read with its topology file.\n+func TestContainerSnapshotParity(t *testing.T) {\n+\tpath, dockerLab := parityLab(t)\n+\tc9sLab := dockerLab\n+\n+\tfor _, node := range []string{\"client\", \"srl1\"} {\n+\t\tcontainer := dockerContainer(t, dockerLab, node)\n+\t\tdocker := aggregatedEventFromContainerSnapshot(&container)\n+\n+\t\tstate, nodeState := c9sNode(dockerLab, path, node)\n+\t\tc9s := c9sContainerEvent(c9sLab, state, nodeState, \"running\", \"running\",\n+\t\t\tmap[string]string{\"origin\": clablabruntime.EventOriginSnapshot})\n+\n+\t\tassertAttributeParity(t, docker, c9s, dockerOnlyContainerAttributes)\n+\t\tgot := mergedEventAttributes(c9s)\n+\t\tif docker.Action != c9s.Action || got[\"origin\"] != \"snapshot\" ||\n+\t\t\tgot[\"state\"] != \"running\" ||\n+\t\t\tgot[\"status\"] != \"healthy\" ||\n+\t\t\tgot[\"network\"] != \"c9s-parity\" {\n+\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s snapshot = %s %v\", node, c9s.Action, got)\n+\t\t}\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+// TestContainerStateUsesDockerVocabulary checks the state and status of every node state c9s\n+// reports, in events and inspect.\n+func TestContainerStateUsesDockerVocabulary(t *testing.T) {\n+\tt.Parallel()\n+\n+\tc9sLab, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(clabcore.WithLabNameOnly(\"parity\"))\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n+\t}\n+\n+\tstate := &clablabruntime.LabState{Name: \"parity\", Namespace: \"c9s-parity\"}\n+\ttests := []struct {\n+\t\tnode          clablabruntime.NodeState\n+\t\tstate, status string\n+\t}{\n+\t\t{\n+\t\t\tclablabruntime.NodeState{Name: \"a\", ContainerState: \"created\", State: \"notready\"},\n+\t\t\t\"created\", \"Created\",\n+\t\t},\n+\t\t{clablabruntime.NodeState{\n+\t\t\tName: \"b\", ContainerState: \"running\", Health: \"starting\",\n+\t\t\tState: \"notready\",\n+\t\t}, \"running\", \"health: starting\"},\n+\t\t{clablabruntime.NodeState{\n+\t\t\tName: \"c\", ContainerState: \"running\", Health: \"healthy\",\n+\t\t\tState: \"ready\", Ready: true,\n+\t\t}, \"running\", \"healthy\"},\n+\t\t{\n+\t\t\tclablabruntime.NodeState{Name: \"d\", ContainerState: \"exited\", State: \"stopped\"},\n+\t\t\t\"exited\", \"Exited\",\n+\t\t},\n+\t}\n+\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n+\t\tcontainer := c9sLab.LabRuntimeContainer(state, tt.node)\n+\t\tif container.State != tt.state || container.Status != tt.status {\n+\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s: %s / %s, want %s / %s\", tt.node.Name, container.State, container.Status,\n+\t\t\t\ttt.state, tt.status)\n+\t\t}\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+// dockerInterfaceEvent is a netlink interface event of a Docker container.\n+func dockerInterfaceEvent(\n+\tcontainer clabruntime.GenericContainer,\n+\taction string,\n+\tsnapshot ifaceSnapshot,\n+\tstats *ifaceStatsMetrics,\n+) aggregatedEvent {\n+\tattributes := interfaceAttributes(&container, snapshot)\n+\tif stats != nil {\n+\t\tinterfaceStatsAttributes(attributes, *stats)\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn aggregatedEvent{\n+\t\tType: \"interface\", Action: action, ActorID: container.ShortID,\n+\t\tActorName: container.Names[0], ActorFullID: container.ID, Attributes: attributes,\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+func c9sInterfaceEvent(\n+\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState,\n+\tnode clablabruntime.NodeState,\n+\taction string,\n+\tiface clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData,\n+) aggregatedEvent {\n+\tkey := state.Namespace + \"/\" + state.Name + \"/\" + node.Name\n+\n+\treturn aggregatedEventFromLabRuntimeEvent(nil, clablabruntime.Event{\n+\t\tType: clablabruntime.EventTypeInterface, Action: action,\n+\t\tActorID: key, ActorName: state.Name + \"-\" + node.Name, ActorFullID: key,\n+\t\tAttributes: map[string]string{\n+\t\t\t\"namespace\": state.Namespace, \"lab\": state.Name, \"node\": node.Name, \"pod\": node.Pod,\n+\t\t\t\"origin\": \"clabernetes\",\n+\t\t},\n+\t\tLab: state, Node: &node, Interface: &iface,\n+\t})\n+}\n+\n+// TestInterfaceEventParity compares the interface events of the lab link (linux eth1, SR Linux\n+// e1-1 with its alias ethernet-1/1), the management interface and loopback.\n+func TestInterfaceEventParity(t *testing.T) {\n+\tpath, dockerLab := parityLab(t)\n+\n+\ttests := []struct {\n+\t\tnode string\n+\t\tdata clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData\n+\t}{\n+\t\t{\n+\t\t\t\"client\",\n+\t\t\tclablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{\n+\t\t\t\tName:      \"eth1\",\n+\t\t\t\tIndex:     7,\n+\t\t\t\tMTU:       9500,\n+\t\t\t\tMAC:       \"aa:c1:ab:56:aa:46\",\n+\t\t\t\tOperState: \"up\",\n+\t\t\t\tType:      \"veth\",\n+\t\t\t},\n+\t\t},\n+\t\t{\"srl1\", clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{\n+\t\t\tName: \"e1-1\", Alias: \"ethernet-1/1\", Index: 7, MTU: 9500, MAC: \"aa:c1:ab:56:aa:47\",\n+\t\t\tOperState: \"lower-layer-down\", Type: \"veth\",\n+\t\t}},\n+\t\t{\n+\t\t\t\"client\",\n+\t\t\tclablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{\n+\t\t\t\tName:      \"eth0\",\n+\t\t\t\tIndex:     4,\n+\t\t\t\tMTU:       1500,\n+\t\t\t\tMAC:       \"02:42:ac:14:14:02\",\n+\t\t\t\tOperState: \"up\",\n+\t\t\t\tType:      \"veth\",\n+\t\t\t},\n+\t\t},\n+\t\t{\"client\", clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{\n+\t\t\tName: \"lo\", Index: 1, MTU: 65536, OperState: \"unknown\", Type: \"device\",\n+\t\t}},\n+\t}\n+\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n+\t\tcontainer := dockerContainer(t, dockerLab, tt.node)\n+\t\tstate, nodeState := c9sNode(dockerLab, path, tt.node)\n+\t\tsnapshot := ifaceSnapshot{\n+\t\t\tIndex: tt.data.Index, Name: tt.data.Name, Alias: tt.data.Alias, MTU: tt.data.MTU,\n+\t\t\tMAC: tt.data.MAC, OperState: tt.data.OperState, Type: tt.data.Type,\n+\t\t}\n+\t\tmetrics := ifaceStatsMetrics{\n+\t\t\tRxBytes: 2000, TxBytes: 3000, RxPackets: 20, TxPackets: 30,\n+\t\t\tRxBps: 8000, TxBps: 12000, RxPps: 10, TxPps: 15, Interval: 2 * time.Second,\n+\t\t}\n+\n+\t\tfor _, action := range []string{\"snapshot\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\", \"stats\"} {\n+\t\t\tvar stats *ifaceStatsMetrics\n+\t\t\tdata := tt.data\n+\t\t\tif action == \"stats\" {\n+\t\t\t\tstats = &metrics\n+\t\t\t\tdata.Stats = &clablabruntime.InterfaceStats{\n+\t\t\t\t\tRxBytes: 2000, TxBytes: 3000, RxPackets: 20, TxPackets: 30,\n+\t\t\t\t\tRxBps: 8000, TxBps: 12000, RxPps: 10, TxPps: 15, Interval: 2 * time.Second,\n+\t\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\tdocker := dockerInterfaceEvent(container, action, snapshot, stats)\n+\t\t\tc9s := c9sInterfaceEvent(state, nodeState, action, data)\n+\t\t\tassertAttributeParity(t, docker, c9s, nil)\n+\n+\t\t\tdockerAttributes := mergedEventAttributes(docker)\n+\t\t\tgot := mergedEventAttributes(c9s)\n+\t\t\tfor key, value := range dockerAttributes {\n+\t\t\t\tswitch key {\n+\t\t\t\tcase \"id\", \"name\", \"lab\", \"origin\":\n+\t\t\t\t\t// the node's own ID, name and lab; the source of the event\n+\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n+\t\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t\tif got[key] != value {\n+\t\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s %s %s: %s = %q, docker %q\", tt.node, tt.data.Name, action, key,\n+\t\t\t\t\t\tgot[key], value)\n+\t\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t\tif got[\"name\"] != \"parity-\"+tt.node || got[\"lab\"] != \"parity\" ||\n+\t\t\t\tgot[\"id\"] != \"c9s-parity/parity/\"+tt.node {\n+\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s %s %s: node attributes %v\", tt.node, tt.data.Name, action, got)\n+\t\t\t}\n+\t\t}\n+\t}\n+}\n+\n+// TestInterfaceEventOmitsUnknownValues checks that values the runtime could not read are left\n+// out: an index of 0 would make clients take two interfaces for one.\n+func TestInterfaceEventOmitsUnknownValues(t *testing.T) {\n+\tt.Parallel()\n+\n+\tstate := &clablabruntime.LabState{Name: \"parity\", Namespace: \"c9s-parity\"}\n+\tev := c9sInterfaceEvent(state, clablabruntime.NodeState{Name: \"client\"}, \"stats\",\n+\t\tclablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{\n+\t\t\tName: \"eth1\", Type: \"veth\",\n+\t\t\tStats: &clablabruntime.InterfaceStats{RxBytes: 1, Interval: time.Second},\n+\t\t})\n+\tgot := mergedEventAttributes(ev)\n+\tfor _, key := range []string{\"index\", \"mtu\", This confirms `core/events/parity_test.go` is a NEW file in this PR. So the entire parity test suite (docker vs c9s) was added by this PR, and it constructs both sides manually — so it can't validate the actual netlink vocabulary.

Now the key question remains: does the netlink library's `LinkOperState.String()` return "notPresent"/"lowerlayerdown" (camelCase/lowercase, matching the OLD c9s behavior of raw sysfs values), or "not-present"/"lower-layer-down" (dashed)?

Evidence in favor of my recollection:
1. vishvananda/netlink mirrors kernel naming. Kernel sysfs operstate values: "unknown", "notpresent", "down", "lowerlayerdown", "testing", "dormant", "up". All lowercase, no dashes. iproute2 prints uppercase with dashes ("LOWER-LAYER-DOWN") — that's iproute2's display transformation.
2. I recall the library source having "notPresent" (camelCase) — let me think about whether it's "notPresent" or "notpresent"... In vishvananda/netlink, there's `LinkOperState.String()`:

Actually, I now recall the exact code from vishvananda/netlink link.go:

```go
func (s LinkOperState) String() string {
	switch s {
	case OperNotPresent:
		return "notPresent"
	case OperDown:
		return "down"
	case OperLowerLayerDown:
		return "lowerlayerdown"
	case OperTesting:
		return "testing"
	case OperDormant:
		return "dormant"
	case OperUp:
		return "up"
	}
	return "unknown"
}
```

Hmm wait, is that right? Let me think about the RFC 2863 names as they appear in the kernel: `IF_OPER_UNKNOWN`, `IF_OPER_NOTPRESENT`, `IF_OPER_DOWN`, `IF_OPER_LOWERLAYERDOWN`, `IF_OPER_TESTING`, `IF_OPER_DORMANT`, `IF_OPER_UP`. The netlink IFLA attribute carries a u8; the string conversion is done by userspace. iproute2's `print_link_flags` uses `oper_state` table:

```c
static const char *oper_states[] = {
	"UNKNOWN", "NOTPRESENT", "DOWN", "LOWER-LAYER-DOWN",
	"TESTING", "DORMANT", "UP"
};
```

And sysfs: `operstate_show` in net/core/net-sysfs.c uses:
```c
static const char *operstates[] = {
	"unknown", "notpresent", "down", "lowerlayerdown", "testing", "dormant", "up"
};
```

So sysfs = lowercase no dashes. The c9s old code reported the raw sysfs value: "lowerlayerdown".

For vishvananda: I'm now trying to recall whether it has its own String(). Yes, netlink has `LinkOperState` with String() — I've seen usage `netlink.LinkOperState(2).String()` produce... I genuinely recall "notPresent" with camelCase in that library. There is a known quirk: vishvananda's String() returns "notPresent" (RFC 2863 style camelCase) for NOTPRESENT and "lowerlayerdown" (kernel style) for LOWERLAYERDOWN. Actually hold on — maybe it returns "notpresent"? 

Let me think about the actual source more carefully. From github.com/vishvananda/netlink link_linux.go / link.go:

```go
// LinkOperState represents the operational state of the interface.
type LinkOperState uint16

// LinkOperState represents the operational state of the interface.
const (
	OperUnknown        = 0x0
	OperNotPresent     = 0x1
	OperDown           = 0x2
	OperLowerLayerDown = 0x3
	OperTesting        = 0x4
	OperDormant        = 0x5
	OperUp             = 0x6
)

func (s LinkOperState) String() string {
	switch s {
	case OperNotPresent:
		return "notPresent"
	case OperDown:
		return "down"
	case OperLowerLayerDown:
		return "lowerlayerdown"
	case OperTesting:
		return "testing"
	case OperDormant:
		return "dormant"
	case OperUp:
		return "up"
	}
	return "unknown"
}
```

I'm now quite sure about "notPresent" — I remember this specific camelCase oddity in the library being mentioned in issues (people surprised that it's "notPresent" not "notpresent"). And "lowerlayerdown" all lowercase (not camelCase despite being typed OperLowerLayerDown). This asymmetry is memorable and real.

So the finding is solid: the c9s mapping converts to dashed forms that match NEITHER the library's String() output ("notPresent", "lowerlayerdown") NOR the raw sysfs values. The docker-side events report "lowerlayerdown"/"notPresent". The parity breaks exactly for the state that occurs when a peer node stops (carrier-down) — the very scenario the robot test exercises. The comment in netlinkOperState ("the way netlink, and so the local runtimes' events, name it") is factually incorrect.

Wait — but one more consideration: maybe the author intentionally chose RFC 2863-ish dashed names and updated all tests/docs to match, and maybe the Docker-side output also... no, the Docker side is pre-existing code that calls attrs.OperState.String(). The parity tests construct docker snapshots manually with the dashed strings, so they'd pass either way — but they'd not represent reality on the docker side.

Reasoning
Confirmed:
1. The robot test asserts `lower-layer-down` for the peer's carrier-down update — but only on the c9s side (the robot test runs the c9s runtime in a real cluster). It cannot compare against a Docker side.

2. `core/list.go:154` — `InterfaceState: attrs.OperState.String()` — this is the pre-existing `inspect` code path for the Docker runtime. So the vocabulary used by the *same product* for `inspect interfaces` with Docker is the netlink library's String() output. This means: if `LinkOperState.String()` returns "lowerlayerdown"/"notPresent" (as I recall), then:
   - `inspect interfaces` with Docker reports state "lowerlayerdown"
   - `inspect interfaces` with c9s reports "lower-layer-down" (via netlinkOperState)
   - The docs claim: "the JSON fields and values (`veth`/`device`, netlink state names) are the same as with Docker" — would be wrong for these two states.
   - Events parity likewise.

This is now a well-supported finding. The only uncertainty is the exact String() values of vishvananda/netlink v1.3.1 — I cannot read the dependency in this environment, but multiple independent recollections (kernel sysfs naming, iproute2 display, library source) point to "lowerlayerdown"/"notPresent". I'll report as P2 (correctness defect in a routine scenario — stopping a peer is everyday lab operation, and the whole PR's purpose is parity) — hmm, or P3? Let me think about impact: the `state` attribute value differs between runtimes for the same physical state. Clients that key on state values (e.g., dashboards watching for lower-layer-down) would need runtime-specific handling, which defeats the PR's parity goal. The docs explicitly promise identical values. It's a value-level mismatch in edge states only ("up", "down", "unknown", "dormant", "testing" all match). I'll rate P2 — it's a demonstrable correctness defect against the PR's own stated goal, triggered by a routine operation (stopping a node / link down), and the fix is a one-line change to the mapping (return the raw sysfs strings, or map to the library's exact strings).

Actually wait — one more consideration on "notpresent" vs "notPresent". The sysfs value is "notpresent" (all lower). If vishvananda returns "notPresent" (camelCase), then even the pass-through of raw sysfs "notpresent" would mismatch Docker's "notPresent". And "lowerlayerdown" — sysfs "lowerlayerdown" matches vishvananda "lowerlayerdown" exactly. So the correct fix for exact parity is to map:
- "notpresent" → "notPresent" (if the library's String() is "notPresent")
- "lowerlayerdown" → "lowerlayerdown" (pass-through, i.e., remove the dash mapping)
- "" → "unknown" (matches library default)

Hmm, so the suggested correction should be: make `netlinkOperState` return exactly what `netlink.LinkOperState.String()` returns (pass through sysfs values, with the one camelCase adjustment if needed), and pin the vocabulary with a test against the library constants. I should phrase the finding carefully: the current dashed names don't match the netlink library's `LinkOperState.String()` vocabulary used by the Docker runtime (e.g., `core/list.go` and interface events); verify and align; the parity tests can't catch this because both sides are constructed from the same literal.

Now, is there a chance the docker-side events also went through some normalization I haven't seen? `interfaceAttributes` uses `snapshot.OperState` from `snapshotFromLink` = attrs.OperState.String() — no normalization. `core/list.go` same. Confirmed.

Let me now also double-check the second potential finding: user-created interfaces inside the node are not reported by c9s (parity gap). Also check `reportedInterfaces` — includes eth0 even when the node has no shell? For stats: yes if listed in /proc/net/dev. For state events: no (no sysfs sample). For InspectInterfaces: eth0/lo skipped when !hasStates. OK.

Also, docs statement: "It reports the interfaces a Docker container of the same node kind has, named as in that container" — overpromise regarding user-created interfaces. P4 docs note.

Now let me also verify the remaining unexamined diff hunks quickly: labruntime_gaps_test.go (1019-1074), clabernetes_test.go (1641-1723), event_parity_test.go rest (2811-3106), events.go diff (3106-3399), manifests/plan/primitives (4114-4174). I have session-summary knowledge of most; let me at least skim the events.go diff hunk (3106-3399) and the manifests/plan/primitives hunks to make sure nothing was missed, plus clabernetes_test.go hunk.
The robot test only asserts the c9s-side value `lower-layer-down`, and `core/list.go:154` (pre-existing) uses `attrs.OperState.String()` directly for the Docker runtime — strong evidence for the vocabulary mismatch finding.
